title.zh: 卷三百十六 列傳第二百〇四 貴州土司
title.raw: 卷三百十六 列傳第二百〇四 貴州土司 Volume 316 Biographies 204: Guizhou Tribal Headmen

sentences.zh: 貴州，古羅施鬼國。

translations.literal: Guizhou—in antiquity the state of the Luoshi Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou was in antiquity the realm of the Luoshi Gui.

sentences.zh: 漢西南夷牂牁、武陵諸傍郡地。

translations.literal: In Han it was land of the Southwestern Yi, Zangge, Wuling, and neighboring commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han it formed part of the southwestern frontier territories of Zangge, Wuling, and adjacent commanderies.

sentences.zh: 元置八番、順元諸軍民宣慰使司，以羈縻之。

translations.literal: The Yuan established the Eight Banners, Shunyuan, and other army-and-people pacification commissioner offices to keep them under loose control.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan set up the Eight Banners and Shunyuan and other pacification commissions for armies and civilians, holding the region under a jimi, or loose suzerainty, regime.

sentences.zh: 明太祖既克陳友諒，兵威遠振，思南宣慰、思州宣撫率先歸附，即令以故官世守之，時至正二十五年也。

translations.literal: After the Ming founder had defeated Chen Youliang and his military prestige reached far, the Sinan Pacification Commissioner and the Sizhou Pacification Superintendent were first to submit; they were ordered to hold their former offices in perpetual hereditary tenure—this was in the twenty-fifth year of Zhizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Ming founder had overthrown Chen Youliang and his armies cast their shadow far afield, the pacification commissioners of Sinan and Sizhou were the first to come over; they were allowed to keep their old titles in hereditary succession. That was in 1365, the twenty-fifth year of the Zhizheng reign.

sentences.zh: 及洪武五年，貴州宣慰靄翠與宋蒙古歹及普定府女總管適爾等先後來歸，皆予以原官世襲。

translations.literal: By the fifth year of Hongwu, the Guizhou Pacification Commissioner Aicui, Song Menggudai, and the female chief steward of Puding Prefecture, Shi'er, among others, came to submit in turn; all were granted their former offices in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In 1372, the fifth year of Hongwu, the Guizhou pacification commissioner Aicui, Song Menggudai, and the female administrator of Puding, Shi'er, and others arrived in succession to pledge allegiance; each was confirmed in his or her former post as a hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 帝方北伐中原，未遑經理南荒。

translations.literal: The emperor was then campaigning north against the Central Plains and had no leisure to administer the southern wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still driving his northern campaigns into the heartland and could not yet turn to governing the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 又田仁智等歲修職貢，最恭順，乃以衛指揮僉事顧成築城以守，賦稅聽自輸納，未置郡縣。

translations.literal: Moreover, Tian Renzhi and others paid annual tribute and were most deferential; therefore the assistant commander of the guard, Gu Cheng, was sent to build a walled post for defense, taxes were left to them to deliver on their own, and no prefectures or districts were yet established.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Renzhi and his peers, meanwhile, sent tribute every year and showed exceptional deference; the court therefore had Assistant Guard Commander Gu Cheng erect a walled garrison, allowed them to remit taxes on their own, and did not yet install regular prefectural administration.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年，思南、思州相仇殺，始命成以兵五萬執之，送京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle, Sinan and Sizhou feuded and killed one another; Cheng was first ordered to take fifty thousand troops, seize them, and send them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 1413, when Sinan and Sizhou fell into mutual slaughter, the court at last ordered Gu Cheng to march fifty thousand men, take the chiefs prisoner, and escort them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乃分其地為八府四州，設貴州布政使司，而以長官司七十五分隸焉，屬戶部。

translations.literal: Their territory was then divided into eight prefectures and four subprefectures; the Guizhou Provincial Administration Commission was established, and seventy-five native offices were placed under it, subordinate to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands were carved into eight prefectures and four departments, a Guizhou provincial administration commission was created, and seventy-five native chieftaincies were attached to it under the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 置貴州都指揮使，領十八衛，而以長官司七隸焉，屬兵部。

translations.literal: The Guizhou regional commander was established, commanding eighteen guards, with seven native offices subordinate to him, under the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: A Guizhou regional military commander was appointed over eighteen guards, with seven native offices placed under his command within the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 府以下參用土官。

translations.literal: Below the prefecture level, native officials were used in mixed fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Below the prefectural level the administration still relied in part on native chiefs.

sentences.zh: 其土官之朝貢符信屬禮部，承襲屬吏部，領土兵者屬兵部。

translations.literal: For these native officials, tribute audiences and credentials fell under the Ministry of Rites; succession fell under the Ministry of Personnel; those leading native troops fell under the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences and seals for these chiefs belonged to the Ministry of Rites, succession to the Ministry of Personnel, and command of native levies to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 其後府並為六，州並為四，長官司或分或合，厘革不一。

translations.literal: Later the prefectures were merged to six and the subprefectures to four; native offices were sometimes divided, sometimes combined, and reforms were not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prefectures were reduced to six and the departments to four, while native offices were split or merged in shifting patterns of administrative reform.

sentences.zh: 其地西接滇、蜀，東連荊、粵。

translations.literal: Its territory bordered Yunnan and Shu on the west and linked with Jing and Yue on the east.
translations.idiomatic: The province bordered Yunnan and Sichuan on the west and met Huguang and Guangdong on the east.

sentences.zh: 太祖於《平滇詔書》言：「靄翠輩不盡服之，雖有雲南不能守也」，則誌已在黔，至成祖遂成之。

translations.literal: The founder said in the 《Pacification of Yunnan Edict》: "If Aicui and his peers are not wholly brought to submission, even possessing Yunnan cannot be held"—thus the plan was already fixed on Qian, and it was fulfilled under the Yongle emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In his 《Pacification of Yunnan Edict》 the founder had written, "Unless men like Aicui are fully subdued, Yunnan itself cannot be held"—the design for Guizhou was already in his mind, and the Yongle emperor brought it to completion.

sentences.zh: 然貴州地皆崇山深菁，鳥道蠶叢，諸蠻種類，嗜淫好殺，畔服不常。

translations.literal: Yet all Guizhou was lofty mountains and deep passes, bird-trails and silkworm-thicket paths; the many barbarian peoples were given to lust and killing, and their submission and rebellion were inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guizhou was nothing but towering ranges and deep ravines, trails fit only for birds and paths wound like silkworm cocoons; its many tribal peoples were prone to excess and bloodshed, and their loyalty shifted without warning.

sentences.zh: 靄翠歸附之初，請討其隴居部落。

translations.literal: When Aicui first submitted, he requested a campaign against the Longju tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after Aicui came over, he asked permission to attack the Longju tribes who opposed him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「中國之兵，豈外夷報怨之具。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Are the armies of China tools for outer barbarians to settle private scores?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The armies of the Middle Kingdom are not weapons for frontier peoples to settle private feuds."

sentences.zh: 」及仁智入朝，帝諭之曰：「天下守土之臣，皆朝廷命吏，人民皆朝廷赤子，汝歸善撫之，使各安其生，則汝可長享富貴。

translations.literal: " When Renzhi came to court, the emperor instructed him: "All who hold the soil are officers appointed by the court; all the people are children of the court. Return and govern them well so that each may live in peace, and you may long enjoy wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: " When Renzhi arrived at court, the emperor told him, "Every man who holds land is an officer appointed by the throne, and every subject is a child of the empire. Go back and govern them well so that all may live in peace, and you will long enjoy wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 夫禮莫大於敬上，德莫盛於愛下，能敬能愛，人臣之道也。

translations.literal: In ritual nothing is greater than revering superiors; in virtue nothing surpasses loving inferiors. To be able to revere and to love—this is the way of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: No ritual surpasses reverence for superiors, and no virtue excels in caring for those below; to revere and to care—such is the duty of a subject.

sentences.zh: 」二十一年，部臣以貴州逋賦請，帝曰：「蠻方僻遠，來納租賦，是能遵聲教矣。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-first year, ministry officials memorialized on Guizhou's arrears in tax; the emperor said: "The barbarian region is remote; that they come to pay rent and tax shows they can follow civilizing instruction.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-first year of Hongwu, the ministries reported Guizhou's tax arrears. The emperor said, "That distant frontier still sends grain and tax shows it is already heeding our civilizing influence.

sentences.zh: 逋負之故，必由水旱之災，宜行蠲免。

translations.literal: The reason for arrears must lie in flood and drought disasters; exemption should be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Arrears must be the work of flood and drought; they should be remitted.

sentences.zh: 自今定其數以為常，從寬減焉。

translations.literal: From now fix the amount as the regular levy and reduce it leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter fix a regular quota and reduce it generously.

sentences.zh: 」二十九年，清水江之亂既平，守臣以賊首匿宣慰家，宜並罪。

translations.literal: " In the twenty-ninth year, after the Qing Shui River rebellion was pacified, defending officials said the bandit chief was hidden in the pacification commissioner's household and that he should be punished as well.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twenty-ninth year, once the Qing Shui River rising was suppressed, local officials urged that the pacification commissioner be punished too, since the rebel leader had been sheltered in his house.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蠻人鴟張鼠伏，自其常態，勿復問。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Barbarians swagger like owls and skulk like rats—this is their constant nature; do not pursue the matter further.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Barbarians bluster and then hide—that is their nature; let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 」明初禦蠻之道，其後世之龜鑒也夫。

translations.literal: " The early-Ming way of governing barbarians—this is a mirror for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the early Ming approach to the frontier—a lesson later rulers might well take to heart.

sentences.zh: ○貴陽思南

translations.literal: ○ Guiyang; Sinan
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang and Sinan

sentences.zh: （思州附）〉

translations.literal: (Sizhou appended) 〉
translations.idiomatic: With Sizhou appended.〉

sentences.zh: 鎮遠銅仁黎平安順都勻平越石阡新添

translations.literal: Zhenyuan, Tongren, Liping, Anshun, Duyun, Pingyue, Shiqian, Xintian
translations.idiomatic: Zhenyuan, Tongren, Liping, Anshun, Duyun, Pingyue, Shiqian, and Xintian

sentences.zh: （金築安撫司附）〉

translations.literal: (Jinzhu Pacification Superintendent appended) 〉
translations.idiomatic: With the Jinzhu Pacification Superintendent appended.〉

sentences.zh: 貴陽府，舊為程番長官司。

translations.literal: Guiyang Prefecture was formerly the Chenfan Native Office.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang Prefecture had formerly been the Chenfan native chieftaincy.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，置貴州宣慰司，隸四川。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu the Guizhou Pacification Commission was established, subordinate to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongwu reign a Guizhou pacification commission was created under Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年改隸貴州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle it was transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1413 it was reassigned to the new Guizhou administration.

sentences.zh: 成化十二年置程番府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chenghua Chenfan Prefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1476 Chenfan Prefecture was established.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年移程番府為貴陽府，與宣慰司同城，府轄城北，司轄城南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing Chenfan Prefecture was moved and renamed Guiyang Prefecture, sharing a city with the Pacification Commission—the prefecture governed the north of the city and the commission the south.
translations.idiomatic: In 1569 Chenfan was renamed Guiyang and shared one walled city with the pacification commission, the prefecture administering the north and the commission the south.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，改為貴陽軍民府。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period it was changed to Guiyang Military-Civilian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli it became Guiyang Military and Civil Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 領安撫司一，曰金築；

translations.literal: It oversaw one pacification superintendent's office, namely Jinzhu;
translations.idiomatic: It had one pacification superintendent, at Jinzhu;

sentences.zh: 領長官司十八，曰貴竹，曰麻向，曰本瓜，曰大華，曰程番，曰韋番，曰方番，曰洪番，曰臥龍番，曰金石番，曰小龍番，曰羅番，曰大龍番，曰小程番，曰上馬橋，曰盧番，曰盧山，曰平伐。

translations.literal: and eighteen native offices: Guizhu, Maxiang, Bengua, Dahua, Chenfan, Weifan, Fangfan, Hongfan, Wolongfan, Jinshifan, Xiaolongfan, Luofan, Dalongfan, Xiaochenfan, Shangmaqiao, Lufan, Lushan, and Pingfa.
translations.idiomatic: and eighteen native chieftaincies: Guizhu, Maxiang, Bengua, Dahua, Chenfan, Weifan, Fangfan, Hongfan, Wolongfan, Jinshifan, Xiaolongfan, Luofan, Dalongfan, Xiaochenfan, Shangmaqiao, Lufan, Lushan, and Pingfa.

sentences.zh: 其貴州宣慰司所領長官司九，曰水東，曰中曹，曰青山，曰劄佐，曰龍裏，曰白納，曰底寨，曰乖西，曰養龍坑。

translations.literal: The Guizhou Pacification Commission oversaw nine native offices: Shuidong, Zhongcao, Qingshan, Zhazuo, Longli, Baina, Dizhai, Guaixi, and Yanglongkeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Guizhou pacification commission itself held nine chieftaincies: Shuidong, Zhongcao, Qingshan, Zhazuo, Longli, Baina, Dizhai, Guaixi, and Yanglongkeng.

sentences.zh: 自蜀漢時，濟火從諸葛亮南征有功，封羅甸國王。

translations.literal: From the Shu-Han period, Jihuo followed Zhuge Liang on the southern campaign with merit and was enfeoffed as king of Luodian.
translations.idiomatic: As early as the Shu-Han, Jihuo had aided Zhuge Liang's southern expedition and was enfeoffed as king of Luodian.

sentences.zh: 後五十六代為宋普貴，傳至元阿畫，世有土於水西宣慰司。

translations.literal: After fifty-six generations came Song Pugui; the line passed to the Yuan's A Hua, who held hereditary territory in the Shuixi Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-six generations later the line reached Song Pugui and, under the Yuan, A Hua, whose family held hereditary lands in the Shuixi pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 靄翠，其裔也，後為安氏。

translations.literal: Aicui was his descendant; the line later became the An clan.
translations.idiomatic: Aicui was of that descent; the house later took the surname An.

sentences.zh: 洪武初，同宣慰宋蒙古歹來歸，賜名欽，俱令領原職世襲。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu he came to submit together with Pacification Commissioner Song Menggudai; he was granted the name Qin, and both were ordered to hold their former offices in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongwu he and the pacification commissioner Song Menggudai submitted together; Aicui received the name Qin, and both were confirmed in their old posts as hereditary offices.

sentences.zh: 及設布政使司，而宣慰司如故。

translations.literal: When the provincial administration commission was established, the pacification commission remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the provincial administration was set up, the pacification commission continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 安氏領水西，宋氏領水東。

translations.literal: The An clan held Shuixi and the Song clan held Shuidong.
translations.idiomatic: The An family ruled west of the river and the Song family ruled east of it.

sentences.zh: 八番降者，皆令世其職。

translations.literal: All who submitted among the Eight Banners were ordered to hold their offices in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Every chief of the Eight Banners who submitted was allowed to keep his post in hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 六年詔靄翠位各宣慰之上。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict placed Aicui above all other pacification commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In 1373 an edict ranked Aicui above every other pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 靄翠每年貢方物與馬，帝賜錦綺鈔幣有加。

translations.literal: Each year Aicui presented local products and horses; the emperor bestowed brocade, silk, and paper money in increasing measure.
translations.idiomatic: Every year Aicui sent tribute goods and horses, and the court answered with ever more lavish gifts of brocade, silk, and banknotes.

sentences.zh: 十四年，宋欽死，妻劉淑貞隨其子誠入朝，賜米三十石、鈔三百錠、衣三襲。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Song Qin died; his wife Liu Shuzhen came to court with their son Cheng and was granted thirty shi of grain, three hundred ingots of paper money, and three suits of clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1381 Song Qin died; his widow Liu Shuzhen came to court with their son Cheng and received thirty shi of grain, three hundred ingots of paper money, and three suits of robes.

sentences.zh: 時靄翠亦死，妻奢香代襲。

translations.literal: At that time Aicui had also died; his wife She Xiang succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Aicui died, and his widow She Xiang inherited the office.

sentences.zh: 都督馬曄欲盡滅諸羅，代以流官，故以事撻香，激為兵端。

translations.literal: Regional Commander Ma Ye wished to destroy all the Luo peoples and replace them with regular officials; he therefore found pretexts to flog Xiang and provoked armed conflict.
translations.idiomatic: Regional Commander Ma Ye hoped to wipe out the Luo chieftains and replace them with regular officials; he trumped up charges against She Xiang and whipped her until war threatened.

sentences.zh: 諸羅果怒，欲反。

translations.literal: The Luo peoples were indeed enraged and were on the verge of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Luo tribes were indeed furious and ready to rise.

sentences.zh: 劉淑貞聞止之，為走訴京師。

translations.literal: Liu Shuzhen heard of it and stopped them, then ran to lodge a complaint at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shuzhen heard of the plot, restrained the tribes, and hurried to the capital to plead their case.

sentences.zh: 帝既召問，命淑貞歸，招香，賜以綺鈔。

translations.literal: After the emperor had summoned and questioned her, he ordered Shuzhen to return, summon Xiang, and bestowed brocade and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned her, then sent Shuzhen home to summon She Xiang and rewarded her with brocade and banknotes.

sentences.zh: 十七年，奢香率所屬來朝，並訴曄激變狀，且願效力開西鄙，世世保境。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year She Xiang led her subordinates to court, also accused Ye of provoking rebellion, and offered to open the western frontier and guard the border for generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: In 1384 She Xiang came to court with her followers, denounced Ma Ye for stirring up revolt, and offered to open roads on the western frontier and guard the border for generations.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜香錦綺、珠翠、如竟冠、金環、襲衣，而召曄還，罪之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and granted Xiang brocade, pearls and kingfisher feathers, a ruyi crown, gold rings, and court robes; he recalled Ye and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, gave She Xiang brocade, pearls, a ceremonial crown, gold rings, and court dress, recalled Ma Ye, and punished him.

sentences.zh: 香遂開偏橋、水東，以達烏蒙、烏撒及容山、草塘諸境，立龍場九驛。

translations.literal: Xiang then opened Pianqiao and Shuidong to reach Wumeng, Wusa, Rongshan, Caotang, and other regions, establishing the nine post stations of Longchang.
translations.idiomatic: She Xiang then opened routes through Pianqiao and Shuidong to Wumeng, Wusa, Rongshan, Caotang, and beyond, and set up the nine Longchang relay stations.

sentences.zh: 二十年，香進馬二十三匹，每歲定輸賦三萬石。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Xiang presented twenty-three horses; the annual fixed tribute was set at thirty thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1387 she presented twenty-three horses, and her annual tax quota was fixed at thirty thousand shi.

sentences.zh: 子安的襲，貢馬謝恩。

translations.literal: Her son Ande succeeded and presented horses in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Ande inherited the post and sent horses in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「安的居水西，最為誠恪。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ande dwells in Shuixi and is most sincere and dutiful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ande, who holds Shuixi, is the most loyal of them all.

sentences.zh: 」命禮部厚賞其使。

translations.literal: " He ordered the Ministry of Rites to reward his envoys generously.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the Ministry of Rites to reward his envoys handsomely.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，的來朝，賜三品服並襲衣金帶、白金三百兩、鈔五十錠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Di came to court and was granted third-rank robes, court dress with gold belt, three hundred taels of white silver, and fifty ingots of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In 1392 Di came to court and received third-rank robes, court dress with a gold belt, three hundred taels of silver, and fifty ingots of paper money.

sentences.zh: 香復遣其子婦奢助及其部長來貢馬六十六匹，詔賜香銀四百兩，錦綺鈔幣有差。

translations.literal: Xiang again sent her daughter-in-law She Zhu and tribal chiefs to present sixty-six horses; an edict granted Xiang four hundred taels of silver and graded gifts of brocade and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: She Xiang also sent her daughter-in-law She Zhu and tribal leaders with sixty-six horses; the court granted her four hundred taels of silver and graded gifts of brocade and banknotes.

sentences.zh: 自是每歲貢獻不絕，報施之隆，亦非他土司所敢望也。

translations.literal: From then on tribute came every year without fail; the grandeur of the court's rewards was not something other native commissions dared hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute arrived every year without fail, and the court's generosity toward them was unmatched among the other native chieftains.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，香死，朝廷遣使祭之，的貢馬謝恩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Xiang died; the court sent envoys to perform sacrifices, and Di presented horses in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In 1396 She Xiang died; the court sent envoys to offer sacrifices, and Di sent horses in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 正統七年，水西宣慰隴富自陳：「祖父以來，累朝皆賜金帶。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhengtong the Shuixi Pacification Commissioner Long Fu petitioned: "From my grandfather's time, successive reigns have all granted gold belts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1442 the Shuixi pacification commissioner Long Fu memorialized, "Since my grandfather's day every reign has granted our house a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 臣蒙恩受職，乞如例。

translations.literal: Your servant has received grace in taking office and begs to receive it according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: I have now received office by your grace and ask the same favor.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋誠之子斌年老，以子昂代，昂死，然代。

translations.literal: At that time Song Cheng's son Bin was old and had his son Ang act in his place; when Ang died, Ran acted in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Song Cheng's son Bin had grown old and let his son Ang serve in his stead; when Ang died, Ran took his place.

sentences.zh: 十四年賜敕隴富母子，嘉其調兵保境之功。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an imperial letter was granted to Long Fu and his mother, praising their merit in mobilizing troops to guard the border.
translations.idiomatic: In 1449 an imperial letter praised Long Fu and his mother for mobilizing troops to defend the frontier.

sentences.zh: 隴富頗驕。

translations.literal: Long Fu became rather arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Long Fu grew arrogant.

sentences.zh: 天順三年，東苗之亂，富不時出兵，聞朝廷有意督之，乃進馬謝罪，賜敕警之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshun, during the eastern Miao rebellion, Fu did not send troops in timely fashion; hearing that the court intended to press him, he presented horses in apology and was granted an admonitory edict.
translations.idiomatic: In 1459, during the eastern Miao rising, Fu failed to march promptly; when he heard the court meant to reprimand him, he sent horses in apology and received a warning edict.

sentences.zh: 富死，侄觀襲。

translations.literal: When Fu died, his nephew Guan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu died, his nephew Guan inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 觀老，子貴榮襲。

translations.literal: When Guan grew old, his son Guirong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Guan grew old and was succeeded by his son Guirong.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳儀以西堡獅子孔之平，由觀與子貴榮統部眾二萬攻白石崖，四旬而克，家自饋餉，口不言功，特給觀正三品昭勇將軍誥。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Chen Yi, to pacify Xibao and Shizikong, had Guan and his son Guirong lead twenty thousand tribesmen to attack Baishiya; they took it in forty days, supplied their own provisions, and did not speak of their merit; Guan was specially granted a third-rank patent as General of Manifest Valor.
translations.idiomatic: To pacify Xibao and Shizikong, Grand Coordinator Chen Yi had Guan and Guirong lead twenty thousand tribesmen against Baishiya; they captured it in forty days at their own expense and claimed no credit, for which Guan alone received a third-rank patent as General of Manifest Valor.

sentences.zh: 初，安氏世居水西，管苗民四十八族，宋氏世居貴州城側，管水東、貴竹等十長官司，皆設治所於城內，銜列左右。

translations.literal: Earlier the An clan had long dwelt in Shuixi, governing forty-eight Miao tribes; the Song clan had long dwelt beside Guiyang city, governing ten native offices such as Shuidong and Guizhu; both set administrations within the city, their titles arrayed left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the An family had ruled Shuixi over forty-eight Miao tribes and the Song family had held the east bank and ten chieftaincies from offices inside Guiyang, their titles ranked on either side of the city.

sentences.zh: 而安氏掌印，非有公事不得擅還水西。

translations.literal: The An clan held the seal and might not return to Shuixi without official business.
translations.idiomatic: The An held the commissioner's seal and could not leave the city for Shuixi except on public business.

sentences.zh: 至是總兵官為之請，許其以時巡歷所部，趣辦貢賦，聽暫還水西，以印授宣慰宋然代理。

translations.literal: At this time the regional commander memorialized on his behalf; he was allowed to tour his jurisdiction in season, hurry tribute delivery, and return temporarily to Shuixi, entrusting the seal to Pacification Commissioner Song Ran as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commander then secured permission for him to tour his domain on schedule, collect tribute, and return briefly to Shuixi while Song Ran of the pacification commission held the seal.

sentences.zh: 貴榮老，請以子佐襲，命賜貴榮父子錦纻。

translations.literal: When Guirong grew old he asked that his son Zuo succeed; an order granted Guirong and his son brocade.
translations.idiomatic: When Guirong aged he asked that his son Zuo inherit; the court granted father and son gifts of brocade.

sentences.zh: 先是，宋然貪淫，所管陳湖等十二馬頭科害苗民，致激變。

translations.literal: Earlier Song Ran had been greedy and licentious; the twelve horse-head officers under him, such as Chen Hu, extorted the Miao and provoked rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Song Ran had been greedy and dissolute; twelve sub-chiefs under him, including Chen Hu, had oppressed the Miao until they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 而貴榮欲並然地，誘其眾作亂。

translations.literal: Guirong wished to seize Ran's territory and incited the crowd to revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Guirong wanted Ran's lands and goaded the rebels on.

sentences.zh: 於是阿朵等聚眾二萬余，署立名號，攻陷寨堡，襲據然所居大羊腸，然僅以身免。

translations.literal: Thereupon Aduo and others gathered more than twenty thousand men, set up titles, stormed stockades, seized Dayangchang where Ran dwelt, and Ran barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Aduo and others then mustered more than twenty thousand men, proclaimed their own titles, stormed fortresses, and seized Dayangchang, Ran's seat; Ran himself barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 貴榮遽以狀上，冀令己按治之。

translations.literal: Guirong hastily reported upward, hoping to be ordered to suppress it himself.
translations.idiomatic: Guirong hurried a report to the capital, hoping to be put in charge of the suppression.

sentences.zh: 會阿朵黨泄其情，官軍進討。

translations.literal: When Aduo's faction revealed the plot, government troops advanced to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Aduo's followers exposed the plot, government troops marched against them.

sentences.zh: 貴榮懼，乃自率所部為助。

translations.literal: Guirong was afraid and then personally led his followers to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Guirong led his own followers to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及賊平，貴榮已死，坐追奪，然坐斬。

translations.literal: When the bandits were pacified, Guirong was already dead and was posthumously stripped of rank; Ran was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, Guirong was dead and his honors were revoked; Ran was condemned to death.

sentences.zh: 然奏世受爵土，負國厚恩。

translations.literal: Ran memorialized that his family had received fiefs for generations and owed the state deep grace.
translations.idiomatic: Ran pleaded that his house had held its fief for generations and owed the dynasty a great debt.

sentences.zh: 但變起於榮，而身陷重辟，乞分釋。

translations.literal: But the rebellion arose from Guirong while he himself faced the gravest penalty; he begged to be distinguished and released.
translations.idiomatic: The revolt, he said, had been Guirong's doing, yet he alone faced execution; he begged for mercy.

sentences.zh: 因從末減，依土俗納粟贖罪。

translations.literal: He was therefore given the lesser sentence and, according to native custom, ransomed his crime with grain.
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was reduced, and by local custom he paid a grain fine in lieu of death.

sentences.zh: 都御史請以貴築、平伐七長官司地設立府縣，皆以流官撫理。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief requested that the lands of the seven native offices of Guizhu and Pingfa be made into prefectures and districts, all governed by regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief proposed turning the territories of seven chieftaincies, including Guizhu and Pingfa, into regular prefectures under appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 巡撫覆奏以蠻民不願，遂寢。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator replied that the barbarian peoples were unwilling, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator reported that the tribes would not accept the change, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 宋氏亦遂衰，子孫守世官，衣租食稅，聽征調而已。

translations.literal: The Song clan also declined; descendants kept their hereditary offices, lived on rents and taxes, and answered only to levies and mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: The Song house declined thereafter; its heirs kept their titles, lived on rents and taxes, and answered only when the court called them to service.

sentences.zh: 時安萬鐘應襲，驕縱不法。

translations.literal: At that time An Wanzhong was due to succeed; he was arrogant, unrestrained, and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: About then An Wanzhong was heir apparent, arrogant and lawless.

sentences.zh: 漢民張純、土目烏掛等導之遊獵，酒酣，輒射人為戲。

translations.literal: The Han subject Zhang Chun and the native officer Wugua and others led him on hunting parties; when drunk he would shoot people for sport.
translations.idiomatic: The Han client Zhang Chun and the native officer Wugua took him hunting; drunk, he would shoot people for amusement.

sentences.zh: 又嘗撻其左右，為所殺。

translations.literal: He also once flogged his attendants and was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Once he beat his attendants and they killed him.

sentences.zh: 無子，其從弟萬鎰宜襲，鎰以賊未獲辭。

translations.literal: He had no son; his cousin Wanyi was the proper successor, but Yi declined on the grounds that the killers had not been captured.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son; his cousin Wanyi was the rightful heir but declined until the murderers were caught.

sentences.zh: 烏掛等遂以疏族幼子普者冒萬鐘弟曰萬鈞告襲，承勘官入其賄，遂暫委鐘妻奢播攝事。

translations.literal: Wugua and others then had a distant clansman's young son Puzhe pose as Wanzhong's younger brother Wan Jun and report for succession; the investigating official took their bribes, and for the time being Wanzhong's wife She Bo was entrusted to administer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wugua then had a distant kinsman's child, Puzhe, pose as Wanzhong's brother Wan Jun and claim the succession; the investigating official took bribes, and Wanzhong's widow She Bo was left in temporary charge.

sentences.zh: 萬鎰悔不立，而恨烏掛之主其謀也，遂以兵襲烏掛，烏掛亦發兵相仇殺，皆以萬鐘之死為辭。

translations.literal: Wanyi regretted not having taken office and hated Wugua for masterminding the plot; he therefore attacked Wugua with troops, and Wugua also raised troops for mutual slaughter, each using Wanzhong's death as his pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyi regretted his delay and blamed Wugua for the intrigue; he attacked Wugua with troops, Wugua answered in kind, and both sides claimed to be avenging Wanzhong.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史上其狀，以萬鎰宜襲，但與烏掛相誣訐，宜各宥輸贖。

translations.literal: The touring censor reported the case upward: Wanyi ought to inherit, but he and Wugua had mutually slandered and accused each other; each should be pardoned upon paying ransom.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor reported the affair: Wanyi was the rightful heir, but he and Wugua had traded accusations; both were to be pardoned on payment of a fine.

sentences.zh: 而梟殺鐘者，並戍純等，受其賄者亦罰治，詔如之。

translations.literal: Those who had decapitated Zhong were to be executed; Zhang Chun and others were banished to frontier service together; those who had taken bribes were also punished and dealt with; an edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The killers of Wanzhong were to be executed, Zhang Chun and his accomplices banished, and the bribe-taking officials punished as well; the throne so ordered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鎰死，子阿寫幼，命以萬銓借襲。

translations.literal: Before long Yi died; his son Axie was young; the court ordered Wan Quan to hold the succession in trust.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wanyi died, leaving a young son Axie; the court let Wan Quan succeed provisionally.

sentences.zh: 萬銓有助平阿向功，提督尚書伍文定為之請。

translations.literal: Wan Quan had merit in helping pacify the Axiong revolt; Grand Coordinator Wu Wending interceded for him.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Quan had helped put down the Axiong rising; Grand Coordinator Wu Wending spoke for him at court.

sentences.zh: 萬銓亦自陳其功，乞加參政銜，賜蟒衣，帝命賜以應得之服。

translations.literal: Wan Quan also himself stated his merit, begging to be given vice-commissioner rank and a python robe; the emperor ordered him given the robes due his station.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Quan memorialized his own service, asking for vice-commissioner rank and a python robe; the emperor granted only the dress appropriate to his rank.

sentences.zh: 後阿寫長，襲職，改名仁。

translations.literal: Later when Axie grew up he took office and was renamed Ren.
translations.idiomatic: When Axie came of age he took the post and was renamed Ren.

sentences.zh: 未幾死，子國亨襲。

translations.literal: Before long he died; his son Guoheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, and his son Guoheng inherited.

sentences.zh: 淫虐，乃以事殺萬銓之子信。

translations.literal: Licentious and cruel, he then on a pretext killed Wan Quan's son Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Depraved and brutal, he killed Wan Quan's son Xin on a trumped-up charge.

sentences.zh: 信兄智與其母別居於安順州，聞之，因告國亨反。

translations.literal: Xin's elder brother Zhi and their mother lived apart at Anshun Prefecture; on hearing it he therefore denounced Guoheng as a rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's elder brother Zhi and their mother lived apart in Anshun; hearing of the murder, Zhi reported Guoheng for rebellion.

sentences.zh: 巡撫王諍遽請發兵誅國亨，智遂為總兵安大朝畫策，且約輸兵糧數萬。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Zheng urgently requested troops be sent to execute Guoheng; Zhi then devised strategy for Regional Commander An Dachao and also undertook to furnish tens of thousands in military grain.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Zheng urgently asked for troops to destroy Guoheng; Zhi drew up plans for Regional Commander An Dachao and promised tens of thousands of rations.

sentences.zh: 及師至陸廣河，智糧不至。

translations.literal: When the army reached the Luguang River, Zhi's grain did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the army reached the Luguang River, Zhi's supplies had not come.

sentences.zh: 諍乃令人諭國亨，而止大朝毋進。

translations.literal: Zheng then sent someone to instruct Guoheng and ordered Dachao not to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng sent an envoy to reason with Guoheng and told Dachao to halt.

sentences.zh: 兵已渡河，為國亨所敗。

translations.literal: The troops had already crossed the river and were defeated by Guoheng.
translations.idiomatic: The army had already crossed the river and was beaten by Guoheng.

sentences.zh: 國亨懼大誅，遣使哀辭乞降，朝廷未之許。

translations.literal: Guoheng, fearing severe punishment, sent envoys with tearful pleas begging to surrender; the court did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing execution, Guoheng sent envoys with abject pleas to surrender; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 巡撫阮文中至，檄捕諸反者，密使語國亨，亟出諸奸徒，割地以處安智母子，還所費兵糧，朝廷當待汝以不死。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Ruan Wenzong arrived, he issued warrants to seize all rebels and secretly told Guoheng to expel the wicked at once, cede land to settle An Zhi and his mother, restore the military grain spent, and the court would spare him from death.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Ruan Wenzong arrived, issued warrants for the rebels, and secretly told Guoheng to hand over his ringleaders, cede territory for An Zhi and his mother, repay the army's grain, and the throne would spare his life.

sentences.zh: 於是國亨悉聽命，帝果赦不誅，而命國亨子民襲。

translations.literal: Guoheng then obeyed in all things; the emperor indeed pardoned him from execution and ordered Guoheng's son Min to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Guoheng obeyed in full; the emperor pardoned him and installed his son Min as heir.

sentences.zh: 國亨事起於隆慶四年，至成歷五年乃已。

translations.literal: Guoheng's affair began in the fourth year of Longqing and ended in the fifth year of Chenli.
translations.idiomatic: Guoheng's troubles had begun in 1570 and did not end until 1577, the fifth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 國亨既革任，日遣人至京納賂，為起復地。

translations.literal: After Guoheng was removed from office he daily sent men to the capital with bribes to pave the way for restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office, Guoheng sent agents daily to Beijing with bribes, angling for reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 十三年，播州宣慰楊應龍以獻大木得賜飛魚服，國亨亦請以大木進，乞還給冠帶誥封如播例。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Bozhou Pacification Commissioner Yang Yinglong received the flying-fish robe for presenting great timber; Guoheng too asked to present great timber and begged restoration of cap, belt, patent, and enfeoffment on the Bozhou precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, Bozhou commissioner Yang Yinglong won the flying-fish robe by presenting great timber; Guoheng asked to do the same and begged restoration of his cap, belt, patent, and enfeoffment after the Bozhou model.

sentences.zh: 既而木竟不至，乃諉罪於木商。

translations.literal: The timber in the end never came; he then shifted blame onto the timber merchants.
translations.idiomatic: The timber never arrived; he blamed the timber merchants.

sentences.zh: 上怒，命奪所賚。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered what had been bestowed withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered his gifts revoked.

sentences.zh: 國亨請補貢以明不欺，上仍如所請。

translations.literal: Guoheng asked to make up the tribute to show he had not deceived; the emperor still granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Guoheng offered a replacement tribute to prove his honesty; the emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年，國亨子疆臣襲職。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli, Guoheng's son Jiangchen succeeded to office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1598 Guoheng's son Jiangchen inherited the post.

sentences.zh: 會播州楊應龍反，疆臣亦以戕殺安定事為有司所案。

translations.literal: When Yang Yinglong of Bozhou rebelled, Jiangchen was also investigated by officials for the matter of killing Anding.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozhou's Yang Yinglong rose in revolt, officials also opened a case against Jiangchen for killing Anding.

sentences.zh: 科臣有言其逆節漸萌者，詔不問，許殺賊圖功。

translations.literal: Some ministry officials said his rebellious bent was gradually sprouting; an edict said not to inquire and allowed him to kill rebels to win merit.
translations.idiomatic: Some censors warned that his disloyalty was growing; the throne told officials to hold their tongues and let him earn merit by fighting rebels.

sentences.zh: 疆臣奏稱：「播警方殷，臣心未白。

translations.literal: Jiangchen memorialized, saying: "The Bozhou alarm is pressing; my heart is not yet cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangchen memorialized: "Bozhou is in crisis, and my loyalty is not yet vindicated.

sentences.zh: 」上復優詔報之。

translations.literal: " The emperor again replied with a gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor answered again with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 巡撫郭子章許疆臣以應龍平後還播所侵水西烏江地六百里以酬功，於是疆臣兵從沙溪入。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang promised Jiangchen that after Yinglong was pacified he would return six hundred li of Wujiang land in Shuixi that Bozhou had encroached on, as reward for merit; thereupon Jiangchen's troops entered by Shaxi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang promised Jiangchen six hundred li of Wujiang country in Shuixi that Bozhou had seized, once Yinglong fell, as payment for his service; Jiangchen marched in through Shaxi.

sentences.zh: 有蜚語水西佐賊者，總督李化龍檄詰之，疆臣遂執賊二十余人，率所部奪落濛關，至大水田，焚桃溪莊。

translations.literal: There was rumor that Shuixi aided the rebels; Governor-General Li Huolong sent a dispatch to interrogate him; Jiangchen then seized more than twenty rebels, led his followers to seize Luomeng Pass, reached Dashuitian, and burned Taoxi manor.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Shuixi was helping the rebels; Governor-General Li Huolong demanded an account; Jiangchen seized twenty-odd men, led his troops to take Luomeng Pass, pushed to Dashuitian, and burned Taoxi manor.

sentences.zh: 應龍伏誅。

translations.literal: Yinglong was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yinglong was put to death.

sentences.zh: 初，應龍之祖以內難走水西，客死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yinglong's grandfather had fled to Shuixi on internal turmoil and died there as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yinglong's grandfather had fled civil strife into Shuixi and died there in exile.

sentences.zh: 宣慰萬銓挾之，索水煙、天旺地，聽還葬，其地遂為水西所據。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Wan Quan held him hostage, demanded the Shuiyan and Tianwang lands, and allowed burial; those lands were then held by Shuixi.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Wan Quan held him for leverage, demanded the Shuiyan and Tianwang territories in return for burial rights, and Shuixi kept the land.

sentences.zh: 及播州平，分其地為遵義、平越二府，分隸蜀、黔，以渭河中心為界。

translations.literal: When Bozhou was pacified, its land was divided into Zunyi and Pingyue prefectures, assigned to Shu and Qian respectively, with the center of the Wei River as boundary.
translations.idiomatic: After Bozhou fell, its territory was split into Zunyi and Pingyue prefectures under Sichuan and Guizhou, bounded by the middle of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 總督王象乾代化龍，命疆臣歸所侵播州地。

translations.literal: Governor-General Wang Xiangqian replaced Huolong and ordered Jiangchen to return the Bozhou lands he had encroached on.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Wang Xiangqian succeeded Huolong and ordered Jiangchen to return the seized Bozhou lands.

sentences.zh: 子章奏言：「侵地始於萬銓，而非疆臣。

translations.literal: Zizhang memorialized, saying: "The encroachment began with Wan Quan, not Jiangchen.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zizhang argued: "The seizure began under Wan Quan, not Jiangchen.

sentences.zh: 安氏迫取於楊相喪亂之時，非擅取於應龍蕩平之日。

translations.literal: The An house pressed for it when the Yang clan was in mourning chaos, not seized on its own when Yinglong was overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: The An took it when the Yang house was in turmoil, not when Yinglong was finally crushed.

sentences.zh: 且臣曾許其裂土，今反奪其故地，臣無面目以謝疆臣，願罷去。

translations.literal: Moreover I once promised him a partition of land; now to seize his old lands back I have no face to answer Jiangchen; I beg to resign.
translations.idiomatic: I myself promised him territory; to seize it back now leaves me ashamed before Jiangchen. I beg to resign.

sentences.zh: 」象乾疏言：「疆臣征番，殲應龍子惟棟不實，首功可知。

translations.literal: " Xiangqian memorialized, saying: "In campaigning against the fan, Jiangchen's claim to have destroyed Yinglong's son Weidong was false; his claim to chief merit is clear.
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Xiangqian countered: "Jiangchen's boast of killing Yinglong's son Weidong was false; his claim to top credit is hollow.

sentences.zh: 至佯敗棄陣，送藥往來，欺君助逆，跡已昭然。

translations.literal: As for feigned defeat and abandonment of the line, and sending medicine back and forth, deceiving the sovereign and aiding rebels, the trail is already plain.
translations.idiomatic: His staged routs, his traffic in medicines with the enemy, his deceit of the throne and aid to rebels—all this is plain.

sentences.zh: 令還侵地，不咎既往，已屬國家寬大。

translations.literal: To order return of encroached land without punishing the past is already the state's generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Demanding the land back while overlooking past crimes is already more than generous.

sentences.zh: 若因其挾而予之，彼不為恩，我且示弱。

translations.literal: If because he held leverage we grant it, he will not regard it as grace and we will show weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Reward his blackmail and he will not feel gratitude; we will only look weak.

sentences.zh: 疆臣既無功，不與之地，正所以全撫臣之信。

translations.literal: Jiangchen having no merit and receiving no land is precisely how to preserve the grand coordinator's credibility.
translations.idiomatic: Deny land to a man without merit, and you preserve the grand coordinator's word.

sentences.zh: 宜留撫臣罷臣，以為重臣無能與蕞爾苗噂沓者之戒。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator should be kept and I dismissed, as a warning that great ministers cannot wrangle with petty Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the grand coordinator and remove me, as a lesson that senior ministers must not haggle with petty chieftains.

sentences.zh: 」於是清疆之議，累年不決。

translations.literal: " Thus the debate over clearing borders went unresolved for years.
translations.idiomatic: " The border dispute dragged on unresolved for years.

sentences.zh: 兵部責令兩省巡按御史勘報，而南北言官交章詆象乾貪功起釁。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War ordered touring censors of the two provinces to investigate and report; north and south remonstrance officials submitted joint memorials condemning Xiangqian for grasping merit and provoking strife.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War ordered censors in both provinces to investigate; memorialists north and south alike denounced Xiangqian for seizing credit and stirring trouble.

sentences.zh: 科臣呂邦耀復劾子章納賄縱奸，子章求去益力。

translations.literal: Ministry official Lü Bangyao again impeached Zizhang for taking bribes and indulging villains; Zizhang pressed harder to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lü Bangyao again accused Guo Zizhang of bribery and sheltering criminals; Guo Zizhang pressed all the harder to quit.

sentences.zh: 象乾執疆臣所遣入京行賄之人與金，以聞於朝。

translations.literal: Xiangqian seized men and gold sent by Jiangchen to bribe in the capital and reported to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangqian arrested Jiangchen's envoys and the gold they carried to bribe officials in the capital and reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 然議者多右疆臣，尚書蕭大亨遂主巡按李時華疏，謂：「征播之役，水西不惟假道，且又助兵。

translations.literal: Yet most in debate favored Jiangchen; Minister Xiao Dafeng then upheld Touring Censor Li Shihua's memorial, saying: "In the Bozhou campaign Shuixi not only granted passage but also aided with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Most opinion still favored Jiangchen; Minister Xiao Dafeng backed Touring Censor Li Shihua, who wrote: "In the Bozhou war Shuixi not only allowed passage but sent troops.

sentences.zh: 矧失之土司，得之土司，播固輸糧，水亦納賦，不宜以土地之故傷字小之仁，地宜歸疆臣。

translations.literal: Moreover lost to one chieftain and gained to another; Bozhou still submits grain and Shuixi still pays tax; we should not harm our kindness to the small because of land; the territory should go to Jiangchen.
translations.idiomatic: Land lost to one native ruler and gained to another changes little: Bozhou still pays grain, Shuixi still pays tax. Do not sacrifice mercy toward the weak over soil; the land should stay with Jiangchen.

sentences.zh: 」於是疆臣增官進秩，其母得賜祭，水西尾大之患，亦於是乎不可制矣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Jiangchen was promoted in rank; his mother received sacrificial grants; and the mischief of Shuixi growing too large became thereafter uncontrollable.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiangchen was promoted; his mother received imperial sacrifices; and from that moment Shuixi's power grew too heavy to manage.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，疆臣死，弟堯臣襲。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year Jiangchen died; his younger brother Yaochen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In year 36 Jiangchen died; his younger brother Yaochen inherited.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，烏撒土舍謀逐安效良，堯臣以追印為名，領兵數萬長驅入滇，直薄沾益州，所過焚掠，備極慘毒。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year, a Wusa native clerk plotted to drive out An Xiaoliang; Yaochen, on the pretext of recovering seals, led tens of thousands of troops in a long drive into Yunnan, pressing straight to Zhanyi Prefecture; wherever they passed they burned and plundered with utmost cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: In year 41 a Wusa clerk plotted to oust An Xiaoliang; Yaochen marched tens of thousands into Yunnan on the pretext of recovering seals, drove on Zhanyi, and burned and looted with terrible cruelty wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方以越境擅兵欲加堯臣罪，而堯臣死。

translations.literal: The court was just about to punish Yaochen for crossing borders with troops on his own authority when Yaochen died.
translations.idiomatic: The court was preparing to punish him for unauthorized cross-border campaigning when Yaochen died.

sentences.zh: 子位幼，命其妻奢社輝攝事。

translations.literal: His son Wei was young; the court ordered his wife She Shehui to administer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei was a child; the court put his wife She Shehui in charge.

sentences.zh: 社輝，永寧宣撫奢崇明女弟。

translations.literal: Shehui was the younger sister of Yongning Pacification Commissioner She Chongming's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Shehui was the younger sister of Yongning commissioner She Chongming's wife.

sentences.zh: 崇明子寅獷悍，與社輝爭地，相仇恨。

translations.literal: Chongming's son Yin was fierce and domineering; he and Shehui quarreled over land and harbored mutual hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Chongming's son Yin was violent and overbearing; he and Shehui feuded over territory and hated each other.

sentences.zh: 而安邦彥者，位之叔父也，素懷異志，陰與崇明合。

translations.literal: An Bangyan was Wei's uncle; he had long harbored disloyal intent and secretly joined with Chongming.
translations.idiomatic: An Bangyan, Wei's uncle, had long nursed treasonous designs and secretly aligned with Chongming.

sentences.zh: 及崇明反，調兵水西，邦彥遂挾位叛以應之，位幼弱不能制。

translations.literal: When Chongming rebelled, troops were mobilized from Shuixi; Bangyan then seized Wei and rebelled in response; Wei was young and could not control him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongming rose, Shuixi mobilized; Bangyan seized the boy Wei and rebelled in concert; Wei was too young to resist.

sentences.zh: 邦彥更招故宣慰土舍宋萬化為助，率兵趨畢節，陷之，分兵破安順、平壩、沾益。

translations.literal: Bangyan further recruited the former pacification native clerk Song Wanhua as aid, led troops toward Bijie and took it, and divided forces to overrun Anshun, Pingba, and Zhanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan enlisted the former pacification clerk Song Wanhua, marched on Bijie and captured it, and sent columns against Anshun, Pingba, and Zhanyi.

sentences.zh: 而萬化亦率苗仲九股陷龍裏，遂圍貴陽，自稱羅甸王，時天啟二年二月也。

translations.literal: Wanhua also led nine Miao zhong companies to take Longli, then besieged Guiyang, styling himself King of Luodian; it was the second month of the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wanhua led nine Miao companies into Longli, then besieged Guiyang as King of Luodian—in the second month of 1622.

sentences.zh: 巡撫李枟方受代，聞變，與巡按御史史永安悉力拒守。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Li Zong was just receiving his successor; on hearing the uprising, he and Touring Censor Shi Yongan strained every effort to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Li Zong was handing over his post when the revolt broke; he and Touring Censor Shi Yongan threw everything into the defense.

sentences.zh: 賊攻不能克，則沿巖制柵，斷城中出入。

translations.literal: When the rebels could not take the city they built palisades along the cliffs and cut off movement in and out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to storm the city, the rebels built cliff palisades and cut off all traffic in and out.

sentences.zh: 鎮將張彥芳將兵二萬赴援，隔龍裏不得進。

translations.literal: Commander Zhang Yanfang led twenty thousand men to relieve them but was blocked at Longli and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhang Yanfang marched twenty thousand to relieve the city but was stopped at Longli.

sentences.zh: 貴州總兵楊愈懋、推官郭象儀與賊戰於江門而死。

translations.literal: Guizhou Regional Commander Yang Yumao and Assistant Magistrate Guo Xiangyi died fighting the rebels at Jiangmen.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou commander Yang Yumao and magistrate Guo Xiangyi were killed fighting at Jiangmen.

sentences.zh: 外援既絕，攻益急，城中糧盡，人相食，而拒守不遺余力。

translations.literal: Outside aid cut off, the attack grew fiercer; grain in the city ran out and men ate one another, yet they defended without sparing effort.
translations.idiomatic: Relief cut off, the assault intensified; grain failed, people ate the dead, yet the garrison held with desperate tenacity.

sentences.zh: 中朝方急遼，不之省。

translations.literal: The central court was absorbed in Liaodong and paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: The court was fixated on Liaodong and took little notice.

sentences.zh: 已，以王三善為巡撫，倉卒調兵食，大會將士，分兵二道進。

translations.literal: Soon Wang Sanshan was made grand coordinator; he hastily mobilized troops and grain, convened officers, and advanced in two columns.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sanshan was appointed grand coordinator; he scrambled for troops and supplies, rallied the commanders, and advanced in two wings.

sentences.zh: 三日抵龍頭營，屢敗賊兵，遂奪龍裏。

translations.literal: On the third day they reached Longtou Camp, repeatedly defeated rebel troops, and recovered Longli.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day they reached Longtou Camp, routed the rebels again and again, and retook Longli.

sentences.zh: 邦彥聞新撫自將大兵數十萬，懼甚，遂退屯龍洞。

translations.literal: Bangyan heard the new coordinator was personally leading hundreds of thousands of troops, was greatly afraid, and pulled back to camp at Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the new coordinator was leading vast armies in person, Bangyan was terrified and fell back to Longdong.

sentences.zh: 前鋒楊明楷率烏羅兵擊死安邦俊，遂乘勝抵貴陽城下，先以五騎傳呼曰：「新撫至矣。

translations.literal: Vanguard Yang Mingkai led Wuluo troops, killed An Bangjun in battle, then pressed in triumph to Guiyang's walls; first five horsemen cried out, saying: "The new coordinator has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguard Yang Mingkai led Wuluo troops, killed An Bangjun, and drove to the walls of Guiyang; five horsemen rode ahead shouting, "The new coordinator is here.

sentences.zh: 」舉城歡呼更生。

translations.literal: " The whole city shouted for joy as if reborn.
translations.idiomatic: " The city erupted as if brought back from the dead.

sentences.zh: 貴陽被圍十余月，城中軍民男婦四十萬，至是餓死幾盡，僅余二百人。

translations.literal: Guiyang had been besieged more than ten months; of four hundred thousand soldiers and civilians, men and women in the city, by then nearly all had starved; only two hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang had been besieged over ten months; of four hundred thousand souls inside, nearly all had starved—only two hundred survived.

sentences.zh: 詳《李枟》及《三善傳》中。

translations.literal: For details see the biographies of Li Zong and Wang Sanshan.
translations.idiomatic: For the full account see the biographies of Li Zong and Wang Sanshan.

sentences.zh: 貴陽圍既解，邦彥遠遁陸廣河外。

translations.literal: Once the siege of Guiyang was lifted, Bangyan fled far beyond the Luguang River.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege lifted, Bangyan fled beyond the Luguang River.

sentences.zh: 三善遣使諭社輝母子縛邦彥以降。

translations.literal: Sanshan sent envoys to urge Shehui and her son to bind Bangyan and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Sanshan sent envoys urging Shehui and her son to bind Bangyan and submit.

sentences.zh: 大軍至者日益眾，三善欲因糧於敵。

translations.literal: Troops arriving daily grew more numerous; Sanshan wished to forage grain from the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements swelled daily; Sanshan planned to live off enemy grain.

sentences.zh: 又諸軍視賊過易，楊明楷營於三十里外。

translations.literal: Also the armies thought the rebels too easy; Yang Mingkai camped thirty li away.
translations.idiomatic: The troops also grew careless; Yang Mingkai pitched camp thirty li out.

sentences.zh: 邦彥復糾諸苗來攻，師敗，明楷為所執。

translations.literal: Bangyan mustered the Miao again to attack; the army was defeated and Mingkai was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan rallied the Miao and struck; the army was routed and Mingkai captured.

sentences.zh: 邦彥勢復張，合眾欲再圍貴陽。

translations.literal: Bangyan's power swelled again; he united his forces intending to besiege Guiyang once more.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan's strength revived; he gathered his hosts to besiege Guiyang again.

sentences.zh: 三善遣兵三路禦之，破生苗寨二百余，擒萬化等，焚其積聚數萬。

translations.literal: Sanshan sent troops in three routes to meet them, destroyed more than two hundred Sheng Miao stockades, captured Wanhua and others, and burned their stores numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Sanshan sent three columns against him, overran two hundred Sheng Miao villages, seized Wanhua and others, and burned stores numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 龍裏、定番四路並通，諸苗畔者相繼降。

translations.literal: Longli, Dingfan, and the four routes all reopened; Miao who had sided with the rebels surrendered in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Longli, Dingfan, and the four routes were reopened; rebel Miao surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 邦彥氣奪不敢出，於鴨池、陸廣諸要地掘塹屯兵，為自守計。

translations.literal: Bangyan's spirit waned and he dared not emerge; at key points such as Yachi and Luguang he dug trenches and stationed troops for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan lost heart and dared not show himself; at Yachi, Luguang, and other choke points he dug trenches and dug in.

sentences.zh: 時奢崇明為蜀兵所敗，計窮投水西，與邦彥合。

translations.literal: At that time She Chongming had been defeated by Shu troops; at wit's end he fled to Shuixi and joined Bangyan.
translations.idiomatic: She Chongming, beaten by Sichuan forces, fled in desperation to Shuixi and joined Bangyan.

sentences.zh: 三年，三善督兵攻大方賊巢，擒土司何中尉等，進營紅崖。

translations.literal: In the third year Sanshan supervised troops attacking the rebel nest at Dafang, captured chieftains such as He Zhongwei, and advanced camp to Hongya.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3 Sanshan led the assault on the Dafang stronghold, captured chieftains including He Zhongwei, and camped at Hongya.

sentences.zh: 連破天臺、水腳等七囤，奪其天險。

translations.literal: In succession he took seven stockades including Tiantai and Shuijiao and seized their natural strongpoints.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed seven forts including Tiantai and Shuijiao and took their natural defenses.

sentences.zh: 別將亦破賊於羊耳，追至鴨池河，奪其戰象。

translations.literal: A detached column also defeated rebels at Yang'er, pursued to Yachi River, and seized their war elephants.
translations.idiomatic: A detached force routed rebels at Yang'er, chased them to the Yachi River, and seized their war elephants.

sentences.zh: 遂深入至紅鳥岡，諸苗奔潰。

translations.literal: They then pushed deep to Hongniao Hillock and the Miao fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed on to Hongniao Hillock and the Miao broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 三善率兵直入大方，奢社輝、安位焚其巢，竄火灼堡，邦彥奔織金。

translations.literal: Sanshan led troops straight into Dafang; She Shehui and An Wei burned their nest, fled through Huozhuo Fort, and Bangyan ran to Zhijin.
translations.idiomatic: Sanshan drove into Dafang; She Shehui and An Wei burned their base, fled through Huozhuo Fort, and Bangyan escaped to Zhijin.

sentences.zh: 位遂遣人赴鎮遠，乞降於總督楊述中。

translations.literal: Wei then sent men to Zhenyuan, begging to surrender to Governor-General Yang Shuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent envoys to Zhenyuan to surrender to Governor-General Yang Shuzhong.

sentences.zh: 許之，令擒崇明父子自贖，一意主撫。

translations.literal: Shuzhong agreed and ordered them to capture Chongming father and son as ransom; he was wholly inclined to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzhong accepted and told them to hand over Chongming and his son as proof of loyalty; he favored appeasement.

sentences.zh: 而三善責並獻邦彥，當並用剿，議不合。

translations.literal: But Sanshan demanded they also present Bangyan and wanted simultaneous suppression; the policies did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Sanshan insisted they deliver Bangyan too and pressed for extermination; the two policies clashed.

sentences.zh: 往返間已逾數月，邦彥得益兵為備。

translations.literal: Back and forth already exceeded several months; Bangyan gained more troops and made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Months of wrangling passed; Bangyan gathered more men and fortified his position.

sentences.zh: 三善糧不繼，焚大方，還貴州，道遇賊，三善為所害。

translations.literal: Sanshan's grain could not keep up; he burned Dafang, returned to Guizhou, met rebels on the road, and was killed by them.
translations.idiomatic: Supplies failed; Sanshan burned Dafang, withdrew toward Guizhou, was ambushed on the road, and killed.

sentences.zh: 邦彥率數萬眾來追，總理魯欽力禦之，大戰數日，大軍無糧，乘夜皆潰，欽自剄。

translations.literal: Bangyan pursued with tens of thousands; Superintendent Lu Qin resisted with all his strength; after several days of great battle the main army had no grain; in the night all fled in rout and Qin cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan pursued with tens of thousands; Superintendent Lu Qin held him off for days, but the army ran out of food, broke at night, and Qin took his own life.

sentences.zh: 賊燒劫諸堡，苗兵復助逆，貴陽三十里外樵蘇不行，城中復大震。

translations.literal: Rebels burned and plundered the forts; Miao troops again aided the rebels; within thirty li of Guiyang no one could gather firewood; the city was shaken again.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels torched the outposts; Miao auxiliaries joined them again; within thirty li of Guiyang no one dared gather fuel; panic returned to the city.

sentences.zh: 初，大方東倚播，北倚藺，相為掎角。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dafang leaned east on Bozhou and north on Lin, each supporting the other as pincers.
translations.idiomatic: Once Dafang had leaned on Bozhou to the east and Lin to the north, each propping the other like pincers.

sentences.zh: 後播、藺既平，賊惟恃烏撒為援，而畢節為四夷交通處。

translations.literal: Later when Bozhou and Lin were pacified, the rebels relied only on Wusa for aid, and Bijie was where the four yi met in communication.
translations.idiomatic: After Bozhou and Lin fell, the rebels had only Wusa for support, while Bijie was the crossroads of the four frontiers.

sentences.zh: 當三善由貴陽陸廣深入大方百七十里，皆羅鬼巢窟，以失地利而陷。

translations.literal: When Sanshan advanced from Guiyang through Luguang deep into Dafang one hundred seventy li, all was Luogui lair; he fell because he lost terrain advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Sanshan's march from Guiyang through Luguang one hundred seventy li into Dafang crossed nothing but Luogui country; he was undone by bad ground.

sentences.zh: 天啟間，朱燮元為蜀督，建議滇兵出沾益，遏安效良應援，分兵於天生橋、尋甸等處，以絕其走；

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period Zhu Xianyuan was Shu governor; he proposed that Yunnan troops leave Zhanyi to block An Xiaoliang's relief, divide troops at Tiansheng Bridge, Xundian, and elsewhere to cut escape;
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi, Sichuan governor Zhu Xianyuan proposed Yunnan troops from Zhanyi to block An Xiaoliang's relief, detachments at Tiansheng Bridge and Xundian to cut retreat,

sentences.zh: 蜀兵臨畢節，扼其交通之路，而別出龍場巖後，以奪其險；

translations.literal: Shu troops would press Bijie and choke their lines of communication, while another force would come out behind Longchang Rock to seize their strongpoints;
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan forces would pin Bijie and sever their routes, while another column would take Longchang Rock from the rear and seize their heights;

sentences.zh: 黔兵由普定渡思臘河，徑趨邦彥巢，由陸廣、鴨池搗其虛；

translations.literal: Qian troops would cross the Sila River from Puding and strike straight at Bangyan's lair, while raiding his rear through Luguang and Yachi;
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou forces would ford the Sila River at Puding and drive on Bangyan's stronghold, while columns through Luguang and Yachi struck his rear;

sentences.zh: 粵西兵出泗城，分道策應；

translations.literal: Guangxi troops would march out from Sicheng in separate columns to coordinate;
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi troops would leave Sicheng in divided columns to support the attack;

sentences.zh: 然後大軍由遵義鼓行而前。

translations.literal: Then the main army would advance from Zunyi with drums beating.
translations.idiomatic: The main army would then march from Zunyi to the roll of drums.

sentences.zh: 尋以憂去，未及用。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on account of mourning and the plan was never adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to observe mourning, and the plan was never used.

sentences.zh: 總督閔夢得繼之，亦以貴州抵大方路險，賊惟恃畢節一路外通。

translations.literal: Governor-General Min Mengde succeeded him; he too held that the route from Guizhou to Dafang was perilous and that the rebels relied solely on Bijie as their one outlet to the outside.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Min Mengde followed him and likewise argued that the road from Guizhou to Dafang was treacherous and that the rebels depended on Bijie as their only outside line.

sentences.zh: 我兵宜從永寧始，自永寧而普市，而摩泥，而赤水，百五十里皆坦途。

translations.literal: Our troops should start from Yongning; from Yongning through Pushi, Moni, and Chishui was one hundred fifty li of open road.
translations.idiomatic: Our forces should begin at Yongning; from Yongning by way of Pushi, Moni, and Chishui stretched one hundred fifty li of level highway.

sentences.zh: 赤水有城郭可憑而守，宜結營進逼。

translations.literal: Chishui had walls one could rely on for defense; a camp should be established there to press forward.
translations.idiomatic: Chishui had walled defenses to hold; a camp should be set there to press the advance.

sentences.zh: 四十里為白巖，六十里為層臺，又六十里為畢節。

translations.literal: Forty li beyond was Baiyan, sixty li to Cengtai, and another sixty li to Bijie.
translations.idiomatic: Baiyan lay forty li on, Cengtai sixty li farther, and Bijie another sixty li beyond that.

sentences.zh: 畢節至大方不及六十里，賊必並力來禦，須重兵扼之，斷其四走之路，然後遵義、貴陽克期而進，亦不果用。

translations.literal: From Bijie to Dafang was less than sixty li; the rebels would surely mass to resist; heavy troops must hold them and cut their four escape routes; only then could Zunyi and Guiyang advance on schedule—this too was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Bijie to Dafang was under sixty li; the rebels would throw their full strength against us, so a strong detachment must choke them and sever their four escape routes before Zunyi and Guiyang could move on a fixed date—and this plan too went unused.

sentences.zh: 及是黔事棘，詔起燮元總督貴、雲、川、廣。

translations.literal: When Guizhou affairs grew critical, an edict recalled Zhu Xieyuan as governor of Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: As Guizhou affairs turned desperate, an edict recalled Zhu Xieyuan to govern Guizhou, Yunnan, Sichuan, and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 於是燮元再蒞黔，時崇禎元年也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xieyuan then took office in Guizhou again; it was the first year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyuan returned to Guizhou; it was Chongzhen year 1.

sentences.zh: 奢崇明自號大梁王，安邦彥自號四裔大長老，其部眾悉號元帥。

translations.literal: She Chongming styled himself King of Great Liang; An Bangyan styled himself Great Elder of the Four Borderlands; all their followers called themselves marshals.
translations.idiomatic: She Chongming proclaimed himself King of Great Liang; An Bangyan called himself Great Elder of the Four Realms; their troops all took the title marshal.

sentences.zh: 悉力趨永寧，先犯赤水。

translations.literal: They threw all their strength toward Yongning and first attacked Chishui.
translations.idiomatic: They hurled their main force at Yongning and struck Chishui first.

sentences.zh: 燮元授意守將佯北，誘深入，度賊已抵永寧，分遣別將林兆鼎從三岔入，王國禎從陸廣入，劉養鯤從遵義入。

translations.literal: Xieyuan instructed the defending generals to feign a northward retreat and lure the enemy deep; once he judged the rebels had reached Yongning, he sent other commanders—Lin Zhaoding in by Sancha, Wang Guozhen through Luguang, and Liu Yangkun from Zunyi.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyuan told the garrison to feign retreat north and draw the enemy in; when the rebels had reached Yongning he sent Lin Zhaoding through Sancha, Wang Guozhen through Luguang, and Liu Yangkun from Zunyi.

sentences.zh: 邦彥分兵四應，力不支。

translations.literal: Bangyan divided his forces to meet them on four fronts but could not hold.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan split his army to answer on four sides but could not sustain the pressure.

sentences.zh: 羅乾象復以奇兵繞其背，急擊之，賊大驚潰，崇明、邦彥皆授首。

translations.literal: Luo Qianxiang again took irregular troops around their rear and struck hard; the rebels panicked and collapsed; Chongming and Bangyan were both beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qianxiang swung irregulars around their rear and struck; the rebels broke in panic; Chongming and Bangyan lost their heads.

sentences.zh: 邦彥亂七年而誅。

translations.literal: Bangyan's rebellion had lasted seven years before he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan's revolt had run seven years before he was killed.

sentences.zh: 燮元乃移檄安位，赦其罪，許歸附。

translations.literal: Xieyuan then issued a proclamation to An Wei, pardoned his crimes, and promised acceptance if he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyuan then proclaimed to An Wei, pardoned his offenses, and offered reinstatement if he submitted.

sentences.zh: 位豎子不能決，其下謀合潰兵來拒。

translations.literal: Wei was a mere boy and could not decide; his followers plotted to rally scattered troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was only a child and could not choose; his men plotted to gather fugitive soldiers and resist.

sentences.zh: 燮元扼其要害，四面叠攻，斬首萬余級。

translations.literal: Xieyuan held the strategic points and attacked from all sides in waves, beheading more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyuan seized the key passes and layered assaults from every side, taking more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 復得向導，輒發窖粟就食，賊益饑。

translations.literal: Guides were found again; troops issued grain from hidden stores and ate; the rebels grew hungrier still.
translations.idiomatic: Guides reappeared; the army opened buried granaries for food; the rebels starved all the more.

sentences.zh: 復遣人至大方燒其室廬，位大恐，遂率四十八目出降。

translations.literal: Men were again sent to Dafang to burn their dwellings; Wei was greatly terrified and led forty-eight sub-chiefs out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Forces were again sent to Dafang to burn houses; Wei was terrified and led forty-eight chiefs out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 燮元奏請許之，報可。

translations.literal: Xieyuan memorialized asking permission; approval came.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyuan memorialized for permission; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 而前助邦彥故宣慰宋萬化之子嗣殷亦至是始剿滅。

translations.literal: Song Siyin, son of Song Wanhua who had earlier aided Bangyan, was only now finally exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Song Siyin, son of Song Wanhua who had aided Bangyan, was at last destroyed.

sentences.zh: 乃以宋氏洪邊十二馬頭地置開州，建城設官。

translations.literal: The Song clan's twelve horse-head lands of Hongbian were made into Kaizhou with a walled city and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Hongbian twelve horse-head territories were made Kaizhou, with walls raised and officials appointed.

sentences.zh: 燮元復遣兵平擺金五洞諸叛苗，水西勢益孤。

translations.literal: Xieyuan again sent troops to pacify rebellious Miao of the five caves of Baijin; Shuixi grew yet more isolated.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyuan again sent troops to pacify the rebel Miao of the five Baijin caves; Shuixi stood more alone than ever.

sentences.zh: 十年，安位死，無嗣，族屬爭立。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Wei died without heirs; clansmen fought over succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Wei died without an heir and kinsmen fought over the succession.

sentences.zh: 朝議欲乘其敝郡縣之。

translations.literal: Court opinion favored seizing the crisis to turn the region into prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion favored using the crisis to replace native rule with prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 燮元奏未可驟，乃傳檄土目，諭以威德，諸苗爭納土獻印。

translations.literal: Xieyuan memorialized that it should not be rushed; he issued proclamations to native headmen, instructing them with majesty and kindness, and the various Miao competed to offer land and surrender seals.
translations.idiomatic: Xieyuan argued against haste, issued proclamations to native headmen blending awe and grace, and Miao leaders vied to offer territory and hand over seals.

sentences.zh: 貴陽甫定，而明亦旋亡矣。

translations.literal: Guiyang had just been stabilized when the Ming dynasty in turn fell.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang had scarcely been secured when the Ming themselves fell.

sentences.zh: 思南，即唐思州。

translations.literal: Sinan was ancient Sin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sinan was the old Sin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋宣和中，番部田祐恭內附，世有其地。

translations.literal: In the Xuanhe period of Song, the tribal leader Tian Yougong submitted and his line held the land for generations.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Xuanhe era the tribal chief Tian Yougong submitted and his house held the land for generations.

sentences.zh: 元改宣慰司。

translations.literal: Under the Yuan it was changed to a pacification commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan converted it into a pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 明洪武初，析為二宣慰，屬湖廣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongwu in the Ming it was divided into two pacification commissioners and placed under Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Ming Hongwu it was split into two pacification commissions under Huguang.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年置思南府，領長官司四：曰水德江，曰蠻夷，曰沿河祐溪，曰朗溪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle Sinan prefecture was established, governing four native-official districts: Shuide River, Manyi, Yanhe Youxi, and Langxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle 11 Sinan prefecture was founded, overseeing four native districts: Shuide River, Manyi, Yanhe Youxi, and Langxi.

sentences.zh: 思州領長官司四：曰都坪峨異溪，曰都素，曰施溪，曰黃道溪。

translations.literal: Sinzhou governed four: Duping Eyi Creek, Dusu, Shixi, and Huangdao Creek.
translations.idiomatic: Sinzhou governed four: Duping Eyi Creek, Dusu, Shixi, and Huangdao Creek.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖起兵平偽漢，略地湖南。

translations.literal: At first, when the founder raised his army to pacify the false Han regime, he subdued Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynastic founder campaigned to overthrow the Chen Han regime, he subdued Hunan.

sentences.zh: 思南宣慰使田仁智遣都事楊琛來歸附，並納元所授宣慰誥。

translations.literal: Sinan Pacification Commissioner Tian Renzhi sent steward Yang Chen to submit and surrendered the pacification patent conferred by the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sinan Pacification Commissioner Tian Renzhi sent steward Yang Chen to submit and returned the Yuan pacification patent.

sentences.zh: 帝以率先來歸，俾仍為思南道宣慰使，以三品銀印給之，並授琛為宣撫使。

translations.literal: Because he had been the first to come over, the emperor let him remain Sinan Pacification Commissioner, gave a third-rank silver seal, and appointed Chen as pacification intendant.
translations.idiomatic: As the first to defect, he kept the Sinan pacification post, received a third-rank silver seal, and Chen was made pacification intendant.

sentences.zh: 思州宣撫使田仁厚亦遣都事林憲、萬戶張思溫來獻鎮遠、古州軍民二府，婺川、功水、常寧等十縣，龍泉、瑞溪、沿河等三十四州。

translations.literal: Sinzhou Pacification Intendant Tian Renhou also sent steward Lin Xian and battalion commander Zhang Siwen to offer the two prefectures of Zhenyuan and Guzhou, ten counties including Wuchuan and Gongshui, and thirty-four prefectures including Longquan and Ruiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Sinzhou Intendant Tian Renhou sent steward Lin Xian and commander Zhang Siwen with the prefectures of Zhenyuan and Guzhou, ten counties such as Wuchuan and Gongshui, and thirty-four sub-prefectures including Longquan and Ruiqi.

sentences.zh: 於是命改思州宣撫為思南鎮西等處宣慰使司，以仁厚為使，俱歲朝貢不絕。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to change the Sinzhou pacification office to the Sinan Pacification Commissioner for the Western Regions and so on; Renhou became commissioner; both presented tribute yearly without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Sinzhou's office was elevated to the Sinan Western Regions Pacification Commission; Renhou became commissioner; both paid tribute every year.

sentences.zh: 二年，仁厚死，子弘正襲。

translations.literal: In the second year Renhou died and his son Hongzheng inherited.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2 Renhou died and his son Hongzheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 帝以思南土官世居荒服，未嘗詣闕，詔令率其部長入朝。

translations.literal: Because the Sinan native officials had long dwelt in remote lands and never visited court, an edict ordered them to bring their chiefs to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sinan headmen had long lived in remote country and never come to court, an edict required them to bring their chiefs to audience.

sentences.zh: 九年，仁智入覲，加賜織金文綺，並諭以敬上愛下保守爵祿之道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Renzhi entered court; he was further granted brocade with woven gold and instructed in revering superiors, cherishing subordinates, and preserving rank and salary.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 Renzhi came to court, received brocade with woven gold, and was taught to revere superiors, care for subordinates, and keep rank and stipend.

sentences.zh: 仁智辭歸，至九江龍城驛病卒。

translations.literal: Renzhi took leave to return but died of illness at Longcheng Post on the Jiujiang route.
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi set out homeward but died of illness at Longcheng post on the Jiujiang road.

sentences.zh: 有司以聞，遣官致祭，並敕送柩歸思南。

translations.literal: The authorities reported it; officials were sent to perform sacrifices and orders were issued to escort the coffin back to Sinan.
translations.idiomatic: Officials reported his death; envoys sacrificed and orders sent his coffin back to Sinan.

sentences.zh: 時思州田弘正與其弟弘道等來朝，帝命禮部皆優賜。

translations.literal: At that time Sinzhou's Tian Hongzheng and his brother Hongdao and others came to court; the Ministry of Rites bestowed favors on all.
