translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde Shi-ca of the Long clan, a woman of the clan, inherited the native judgeship, went to the capital to pay tribute, and the emperor praised her.
translations.idiomatic: In 1506 Shi-ca, a Long clanswoman who succeeded as native judge, tribute at court won imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 或曰適擦亦暢妾雲。

translations.literal: Some say Shi-ca was also Chang's concubine Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Some accounts identify Shi-ca with Chang's concubine Yun.

sentences.zh: 西堡阿得、獅子孔阿江二種，皆革僚也。

translations.literal: The two groups A-de of Xibao and A-jiang of Shizikong were both Gelao.
translations.idiomatic: Xibao's A-de and Shizikong's A-jiang peoples were Gelao.

sentences.zh: 初據滄浪六寨，不供常賦。

translations.literal: At first they held the six stockades of Canglang and did not supply regular levies.
translations.idiomatic: They originally held Canglang's six stockades and paid no regular taxes.

sentences.zh: 土官溫愷懼罪自縊，其子廷玉請免賦，不允。

translations.literal: Native official Wen Kai feared punishment and hanged himself; his son Tingyu begged exemption from levies, which was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Native officer Wen Kai, fearing punishment, hanged himself; son Tingyu's plea for tax relief was denied.

sentences.zh: 往征，為其寨長乜呂等所殺。

translations.literal: When troops were sent to punish them they were killed by stockade head Nie-lü and others.
translations.idiomatic: A punitive expedition was ambushed; stockade chief Nie-lü and others killed Tingyu.

sentences.zh: 六年，廷玉弟廷瑞訴於守臣，會乜呂死，指揮楊仁撫其眾。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Tingyu's younger brother Tingrui complained to the defending officials; as Nie-lü had died, Commander Yang Ren pacified the masses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1491 brother Tingrui appealed to local officials; with Nie-lü dead, Commander Yang Ren pacified the tribe.

sentences.zh: 巡撫蕭翀請令其輸賦，免用兵，從之。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Xiao Chong requested that they pay levies and troops be spared; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xiao Chong secured their tax payments in lieu of military action.

sentences.zh: 都勻，元曰都雲。

translations.literal: Duyun—in Yuan it was called Duyun.
translations.idiomatic: Duyun was known in Yuan times as Duyun.

sentences.zh: 洪武十九年置都勻安撫司。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Hongwu the Duyun Pacification Superintendent's office was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1386 the Duyun pacification office was founded.

sentences.zh: 二十九年改為軍民指揮使司，屬四川。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year it was changed to an army-and-civilian commander's office, subordinate to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1396 it became an army-civilian command under Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年改隸貴州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle it was transferred to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1413 jurisdiction shifted to Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治七年置府，領州二，曰麻哈，曰獨山，即合江洲陳蒙爛土長官司地。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Hongzhi a prefecture was established, overseeing two subprefectures, Maoha and Dushan—that is, the territory of the Chenmenglantou native chieftaincy of Hejiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1494 a prefecture was created with subprefectures Maoha and Dushan on former Hejiang Chenmenglantou lands.

sentences.zh: 領縣一，曰清平，即清平長官司地也。

translations.literal: It oversaw one county, Qingping—that is, the territory of the Qingping native chieftaincy.
translations.idiomatic: It also governed Qingping County on Qingping chieftaincy lands.

sentences.zh: 領長官司八：屬府者曰都勻，曰平浪，曰邦水，曰平州六洞；

translations.literal: It oversaw eight native chieftaincies: subordinate to the prefecture were Duyun, Pinglang, Bangshui, and Pingzhou Liudong;
translations.idiomatic: Eight native offices fell under it: Duyun, Pinglang, Bangshui, and Pingzhou Liudong under the prefecture;

sentences.zh: 屬獨山者曰九名九姓，曰豐寧；

translations.literal: subordinate to Dushan were Jiuming Jiuxing and Fengning;
translations.idiomatic: under Dushan, Jiuming Jiuxing and Fengning;

sentences.zh: 屬麻哈者曰樂平，曰平定。

translations.literal: subordinate to Maoha were Yueping and Pingding.
translations.idiomatic: under Maoha, Yueping and Pingding.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十二年，都督何福奏討都勻叛苗，斬四千七百余級，擒獲六千三百九十余人，收降寨洞一百五十二處。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Hongwu Commissioner He Fu memorialized on suppressing rebellious Miao of Duyun, beheading more than four thousand seven hundred, capturing more than six thousand three hundred ninety persons, and receiving the surrender of one hundred fifty-two stockades and caves.
translations.idiomatic: In 1389 Commissioner He Fu reported suppressing Duyun rebels: 4,700 beheaded, 6,390 captured, 152 stockades surrendered.

sentences.zh: 二十三年城都勻衛，命指揮同知董庸守之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Duyun Guard was walled; Commander Assistant Dong Yong was ordered to defend it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1390 Duyun Guard was fortified under Assistant Commander Dong Yong.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，九名九姓蠻亂，命何福平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Jiuming Jiuxing barbarians rebelled; He Fu was ordered to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1392 the Jiuming Jiuxing tribes rebelled; He Fu pacified them.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，豐寧三藍等寨亂，命顧成平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Fengning Sanlan and other stockades rebelled; Gu Cheng was ordered to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1395 Fengning's Sanlan stockades rose; Gu Cheng suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，平浪蠻殺土官王應名，都指揮程暹平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Pinglang barbarians killed native official Wang Yingming; Regional Commander Cheng Xian pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1396 Pinglang tribes killed chieftain Wang Yingming; Cheng Xian restored order.

sentences.zh: 應名妻吳攜九歲子阿童來訴，詔予襲。

translations.literal: Yingming's wife Wu brought their nine-year-old son A-tong to plead; an edict granted him succession.
translations.idiomatic: Widow Wu brought nine-year-old son A-tong to court and secured his inheritance.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年，鎮遠侯顧成招諭合江州十五寨來歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongle the Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Cheng induced fifteen stockades of Hejiang Prefecture to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1406 Marquis Gu Cheng won fifteen Hejiang stockades to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年，陳蒙爛土長官司張鏞奏：「夭壩幹賊首賫果侵掠，請於所侵大陳、大步等寨設一司，隸安寧宣撫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua Zhang Yong of the Chenmenglantou native chieftaincy memorialized: "The Yaobaigan bandit leader Guiguo has raided; I request establishing one office at the invaded stockades Dachen and Dabu, subordinate to the Anning Pacification Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1478 Chenmenglantou chieftain Zhang Yong asked to place a new office over Dachen and Dabu, raided by Yaobaigan chief Guiguo, under Anning pacification.

sentences.zh: 」而豐寧長官司楊泰亦奏峰峒陸光翁等聚爛土為亂。

translations.literal: " Fengning chieftain Yang Tai also memorialized that Lugu Dong Lu Guangweng and others had gathered Lantou for disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Fengning chieftain Yang Tai reported Lugu Dong's Lu Guangweng rallying Lantou rebels.

sentences.zh: 先是，宣慰楊輝平夭壩幹後，即灣溪立安寧宣撫司。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Pacification Commissioner Yang Hui pacified Yaobaigan he immediately established the Anning Pacification Superintendent's office at Wanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After Pacification Commissioner Yang Hui had crushed Yaobaigan he set up Anning pacification at Wanxi.

sentences.zh: 爛土諸苗惡其逼己，至是果等既攻陷夭漂，遂圍豐寧。

translations.literal: The Lantou Miao hated being pressed by him; at this time Guiguo and others having stormed Yaopiao then besieged Fengning.
translations.idiomatic: Lantou Miao resented Yang Hui's pressure; Guiguo, having taken Yaopiao, now besieged Fengning.

sentences.zh: 時輝已致仕，子愛承襲，力弗支，求援於川、貴二鎮。

translations.literal: At the time Hui had retired; his son Ai had succeeded; strength was insufficient; he sought aid from the Sichuan and Guizhou garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Yang Hui's heir Ai, overmatched, appealed to Sichuan and Guizhou garrisons.

sentences.zh: 各奏聞，命仍起輝，會兵討之。

translations.literal: Each reported it; he was ordered to recall Hui and unite forces to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Both provinces reported in; Yang Hui was recalled to lead a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 十六年，鏞復奏賫果糾合九姓、豐寧並荔波賊萬人，攻剽愈亟。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Yong again memorialized that Guiguo had mustered Jiuming, Fengning, and Libo bandits numbering ten thousand men and raided ever more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: In 1480 Zhang Yong reported Guiguo rallying 10,000 men from Jiuming, Fengning, and Libo for fiercer raids.

sentences.zh: 帝責諸守臣玩寇。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked the defending officials for treating bandits lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor scolded local commanders for negligence.

sentences.zh: 於是巡撫謝杲言：「自天順四年以來，諸苗攻劫舟溪等處，不靖至今。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Coordinator Xie Gao said: "Since the fourth year of Tianshun the various Miao have attacked and raided Zhouxi and other places; unrest continues to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Xie Gao noted that since 1460 Miao raids on Zhouxi and elsewhere had never ceased.

sentences.zh: 」乃命鎮守太監張成、總兵吳經相機剿撫。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Garrison Eunuch Zhang Cheng and Supreme Commander Wu Jing to suppress and pacify as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison Eunuch Zhang Cheng and Supreme Commander Wu Jing were told to suppress or pacify as needed.

sentences.zh: 二十年，爛土苗賊龍洛道潛號稱王，聲言犯都勻、清平諸衛。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the Lantou Miao bandit Long Luodao secretly styled himself king, declaring he would invade Duyun, Qingping, and other guards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1484 Lantou rebel Long Luodao secretly proclaimed himself king and threatened Duyun and Qingping guards.

sentences.zh: 豐寧長官楊泰與土目楊和有隙，誘廣西泗城州農民九千，於銕坑等一百余寨殺掠，於是苗患愈盛。

translations.literal: Fengning chieftain Yang Tai had a rift with native clerk Yang He; he induced nine thousand farmers of Guangxi's Sicheng Prefecture to kill and plunder at more than one hundred stockades including Tieken; thus Miao troubles grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: Fengning chief Yang Tai, feuding with clerk Yang He, hired 9,000 Sicheng farmers to raid 100-plus stockades including Tieken, worsening the crisis.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，苗賊七千人攻圍楊安堡，都指揮劉英統兵覘之，為所困。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi Miao bandits seven thousand strong besieged Yang'an Fort; Regional Commander Liu Ying led troops to reconnoiter and was trapped.
translations.idiomatic: In 1489 7,000 Miao besieged Yang'an Fort; Liu Ying's reconnaissance party was trapped.

sentences.zh: 命鎮巡官往援，乃得出。

translations.literal: He ordered garrison and touring officials to go to rescue; only then could they get out.
translations.idiomatic: Relief from garrison officials freed them.

sentences.zh: 五年命鎮遠侯顧溥率官兵八萬人，巡撫鄧廷瓚提督軍務，太監江德監諸軍，往征之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he ordered the Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Pu to lead eighty thousand government troops, Grand Coordinator Deng Tingzan to supervise military affairs, and Eunuch Jiang De to oversee the armies, to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1492 Marquis Gu Pu took 80,000 troops under Grand Coordinator Deng Tingzan and Eunuch Jiang De.

sentences.zh: 七年，諸軍分道進剿，令熟苗詐降於賊，誘令入寇，伏兵擒之，直搗其巢，凡破一百十余寨，以捷聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the armies advanced by separate routes to suppress them; they ordered assimilated Miao to feign surrender to the bandits, lure them to raid, ambush and capture them, strike straight at their nests; in all more than one hundred ten stockades were broken; victory was reported.
translations.idiomatic: In 1494 columns advanced; loyal Miao feigned defection, lured rebels into ambush, and over 110 stockades fell.

sentences.zh: 於是開置都勻府及獨山、麻哈二州。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Duyun prefecture and the Dushan and Maoha subprefectures were newly established.
translations.idiomatic: Duyun Prefecture and Dushan and Maoha subprefectures were then created.

sentences.zh: 正德三年，都勻長官司吳欽與其族吳敏爭襲仇殺，鎮巡以聞，言：「欽之祖賴洪武間立功為長官，陣亡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengde Duyun chieftain Wu Qin and his clansman Wu Min fought over succession and killed each other; the garrison reported it, saying: "Qin's ancestor in the Hongwu period earned merit as chieftain and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In 1508 Duyun chiefs Wu Qin and Wu Min killed each other over succession; officials noted Qin's ancestor had died fighting for the Ming in Hongwu.

sentences.zh: 子琮幼，弟貴署之。

translations.literal: Son Cong was young; younger brother Gui acted in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Young heir Cong had been deputized by uncle Gui.

sentences.zh: 及琮長，仍襲，傳至欽三世。

translations.literal: When Cong grew up he still inherited; the line passed to Qin for three generations.
translations.idiomatic: Cong later succeeded and the line reached Qin in the third generation.

sentences.zh: 敏不得以貴故妄爭。

translations.literal: Min could not vainly contend because of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Min had no claim to dispute Gui's regency.

sentences.zh: 」詔可之。

translations.literal: " The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The court upheld Qin.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十五年，平浪叛苗王聰攻奪凱口屯，執參將李佑等。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jiajing the rebellious Miao of Pinglang Wang Cong attacked and seized Kaikou colony, capturing Assistant Commander Li You and others.
translations.idiomatic: In 1536 Pinglang rebel Wang Cong seized Kaikou colony and took Assistant Commander Li You captive.

sentences.zh: 初，王阿向先世為土官，為王仲武先人所奪，至阿向，與仲武爭印煽亂。

translations.literal: At first Wang A-xiang's forebears had been native officials; they were seized by Wang Zhongwu's forebears; reaching A-xiang, he and Zhongwu fought over seals and incited disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Wang A-xiang's ancestors had been native officers until Wang Zhongwu's line dispossessed them; A-xiang and Zhongwu now fought over seals and stirred revolt.

sentences.zh: 總兵楊仁、巡撫陳克宅平之，斬阿向等，盡逐其黨，以地屬都勻府，改名滅苗鎮。

translations.literal: Supreme Commander Yang Ren and Grand Coordinator Chen Kezhai pacified them, beheaded A-xiang and others, entirely expelled their party, and placed the land under Duyun Prefecture, renaming it Miemiao Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ren and Chen Kezhai executed A-xiang, expelled his faction, annexed the land to Duyun as Miemiao Fort.

sentences.zh: 仲武因諸苗失業，陰為招復，旋科索之。

translations.literal: Zhongwu because the various Miao lost livelihood secretly recruited them back and soon extorted levies from them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu secretly re-enrolled displaced Miao, then taxed them harshly.

sentences.zh: 諸苗不勝怨，遂推阿向余孽王聰、王佑為主。

translations.literal: The various Miao could not bear resentment; they therefore promoted A-xiang's remnant Wang Cong and Wang You as leaders.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes, desperate, rallied A-xiang's heirs Wang Cong and Wang You.

sentences.zh: 巡按楊春芳遣李佑等撫諭之，賊質佑等，乞還土田官印，乃釋佑。

translations.literal: Touring Censor Yang Chunfang sent Li You and others to pacify them; the bandits held You and others hostage, begged return of native fields and official seals, and then released You.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yang Chunfang sent Li You to negotiate; rebels held hostages until fields and seals were promised, then freed You.

sentences.zh: 春芳以聞，詔巡撫調官軍三萬人集屯下。

translations.literal: Chunfang reported it; an edict ordered the grand coordinator to gather thirty thousand government troops at Xiadian.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfang's report brought orders to mass 30,000 troops at Xiadian.

sentences.zh: 屯故絕險，其要害處置弩樓，疊石為防。

translations.literal: The colony was inherently extremely perilous; at its critical points crossbow towers were placed and stones stacked for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Xiadian's cliffs got crossbow towers and stone barriers.

sentences.zh: 攻之三月不克，復調宣慰安萬銓兵合剿。

translations.literal: Attacking three months without success, troops of Pacification Commissioner An Wanqian were again transferred for combined suppression.
translations.idiomatic: After three fruitless months, An Wanqian's pacification troops joined the siege.

sentences.zh: 萬銓力戰破賊，聰等皆伏誅，前後斬首二百六十余級，降苗寨一百五十余，男婦二萬余口。

translations.literal: Wanqian fought fiercely and broke the bandits; Cong and others were all executed; in all more than two hundred sixty were beheaded, one hundred fifty-odd Miao stockades surrendered, and more than twenty thousand men and women.
translations.idiomatic: Wanqian broke the rebels; Cong was executed with 260 others; 150 stockades and 20,000 people submitted.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，敘功賞賚有差。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, rewards were graded by merit.
translations.idiomatic: Victory brought graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 又有黑苗曰夭漂者，在湖、貴、川、廣界，與者亞鼎足居。

translations.literal: There were also Black Miao called Yaopiao, on the borders of Huguang, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Guang, living in tripartite balance with Zheya.
translations.idiomatic: Black Miao called Yaopiao straddled Huguang, Guizhou, Sichuan, and Guang, counterbalancing Zheya.

sentences.zh: 萬歷六年，夭漂請內附。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli Yaopiao requested inner submission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1578 Yaopiao sought incorporation.

sentences.zh: 都御史遣指揮郭懷恩及長官金篆往問狀，而阻於者亞，乃遠從丹彰間道通夭漂。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief dispatched Commander Guo Huai'en and chieftain Jin Zhuan to inquire, but was blocked by Zheya; he therefore went far by the Danzhang bypath to reach Yaopiao.
translations.idiomatic: The censor sent Guo Huai'en and Jin Zhuan, but Zheya blocked the route until they detoured through Danzhang to Yaopiao.

sentences.zh: 會苗坪、黨銀等亦以格於者亞不得通，都御史王緝遣使責者亞部長阿鬥。

translations.literal: When Miaoping, Dangyin, and others also could not get through because of Zheya, Censor-in-Chief Wang Ji dispatched envoys to rebuke Zheya headman A-dou.
translations.idiomatic: Miaoping and Dangyin were likewise cut off; Censor Wang Ji rebuked Zheya chief A-dou.

sentences.zh: 鬥願歸附平定，緝謂鬥故養善牌部，何故欲屬平定，必有他謀。

translations.literal: Dou wished to submit to Pingding; Ji said Dou was originally of the Yangshanpai division—why wish to belong to Pingding? There must be another plot.
translations.idiomatic: Dou sought Pingding jurisdiction; Ji suspected the Yangshanpai chief of plotting mischief.

sentences.zh: 下吏按驗，果得實，蓋欲往平定借諸蒙兵襲養善，皆內地奸人夭金貴等導之。

translations.literal: Lower officials investigated and verified the facts: they wished to go to Pingding to borrow Meng troops to raid Yangshan—all guided by interior traitors Tian Jingui and others.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation proved a scheme to borrow Pingding troops against Yangshan, instigated by traitor Tian Jingui.

sentences.zh: 遂治金貴罪，以者亞仍屬養善，路遂通。

translations.literal: Jingui was punished accordingly; Zheya still belonged to Yangshan; the road was then open.
translations.idiomatic: Jingui was punished; Zheya stayed under Yangshan and routes reopened.

sentences.zh: 於是苗坪、夭漂皆請奉貢賦，比編氓，名其地曰歸化，隸都勻府。

translations.literal: Thereupon Miaoping and Yaopiao all requested to offer tribute and taxes like registered commoners; their territory was named Guihua, subordinate to Duyun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Miaoping and Yaopiao then paid taxes as subjects; their lands were named Guihua under Duyun.

sentences.zh: 凡使命往來，自生齒以上，悉跪拜迎送，夾騶從行，前吹蘆笙，唱蠻歌，呼導而馳。

translations.literal: Whenever envoys came and went, all from those with teeth upward knelt in bowing to welcome and send off, flanked by outriders, blowing reed pipes ahead, singing barbarian songs, calling guidance and galloping.
translations.idiomatic: Official visits were met with kneeling welcomes, escorts, reed pipes, and Miao songs along the road.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝嘉之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended their submission.

sentences.zh: 七年，者亞、阿鬥以反誅，乃罷樂平吏目，增設麻哈州州判一員，令居樂平司，以養鵝、者亞、羊腸諸苗屬之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Zheya and A-dou were executed for rebellion; the Yueping clerk post was abolished and a Maoha subprefecture vice magistrate was added, stationed at Yueping office, with the Miao of Yang'e, Zheya, Yangchang, and others subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1579 Zheya and A-dou were executed; a Maoha vice magistrate at Yueping oversaw Yang'e, Zheya, and Yangchang Miao.

sentences.zh: 初，者亞、阿鬥反，答幹寨阿其應之。

translations.literal: At first when Zheya and A-dou rebelled, A-qi of Dagans stockade responded.
translations.idiomatic: Dagans stockade's A-qi had backed Zheya and A-dou's revolt.

sentences.zh: 鬥誅，阿其屢犯順。

translations.literal: When Dou was executed A-qi repeatedly violated order.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou's death A-qi kept raiding.

sentences.zh: 十四年，土舍吳楠、王國聘慮阿其叵測禍及己，請以答幹、雞賈、甲多諸寨屬蒙詔，立宣威營，歲輸賦。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year native clerks Wu Nan and Wang Guopin, fearing A-qi's unpredictability would harm them, requested that Dagans, Jijia, Jiadu, and other stockades belong to Mengzhao, establishing Xuanwei Camp with annual levies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1586 clerks Wu Nan and Wang Guopin, fearing A-qi, asked to place Dagans, Jijia, and Jiadu under Mengzhao's Xuanwei Camp with taxes.

sentences.zh: 獨阿其不服，引者亞殘苗圍宣威營大噪，曰：「此我地，誰令爾營此？

translations.literal: Only A-qi would not submit; he led remnant Zheya Miao to surround Xuanwei Camp with great clamor, saying: "This is my land—who told you to camp here?
translations.idiomatic: A-qi alone refused, besieging Xuanwei Camp shouting that the land was his.

sentences.zh: 」蒙詔常征秋稅，阿其度使至，以血釁門，令勿通。

translations.literal: " Mengzhao regularly collected autumn grain; A-qi when expecting envoys smeared blood on the gate and ordered no passage.
translations.idiomatic: He barred Mengzhao's tax collectors with blood-daubed gates.

sentences.zh: 居常張傘鼓角，繪龍鳳器，遂與雞賈、甲多、仰枯諸苗擊牛酒為誓，劫歸化，官兵不敢近。

translations.literal: In ordinary times he displayed umbrellas, horns, and drums and painted dragon-phoenix vessels; then with Jijia, Jiadu, Yangku, and other Miao he slaughtered cattle and wine in oath, raided Guihua, and government troops dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: He flaunted regalia, swore with Jijia and allies, raided Guihua, and troops hesitated to approach.

sentences.zh: 獨山土吏蒙天眷願以兵進剿，乃使人佯言，漢已黜蒙詔，令以宣威營地還阿其，旦暮撤兵去矣。

translations.literal: Dushan clerk Meng Tianjuan wished to advance with troops; he therefore sent men falsely saying the Han had dismissed Mengzhao, ordering return of Xuanwei Camp land to A-qi, and that troops would withdraw morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Tianjuan feigned that Mengzhao was dismissed and Xuanwei land would revert to A-qi.

sentences.zh: 阿其乃親馳樂邦牛場诇視，言人人同，遂弛備。

translations.literal: A-qi himself galloped to Lebang Niuchang to spy; everyone said the same; he therefore relaxed defenses.
translations.idiomatic: A-qi inspected Lebang market, heard the same story, and let his guard down.

sentences.zh: 天眷驟入，斬阿其，雞賈、甲多皆降。

translations.literal: Tianjuan suddenly entered, beheaded A-qi; Jijia and Jiadu all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjuan struck suddenly, killed A-qi, and Jijia and Jiadu submitted.

sentences.zh: 其屬蒙詔者，自答幹、雞賈、甲多外，有塘蛙、當井、鬥坡等十七寨。

translations.literal: Those belonging to Mengzhao, besides Dagans, Jijia, and Jiadu, had Tangwa, Dangjing, Doupo, and seventeen other stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzhao held Dagans, Jijia, Jiadu, and 17 more stockades including Tangwa.

sentences.zh: 小橋熟苗龍木恰視寨事，年老，子俸襲，頒糧者遂不及恰，恰輒奪俸之有以為養。

translations.literal: The minor-bridge assimilated Miao Long Muqia oversaw stockade affairs; old in years, son Feng inherited; grain distributors then did not reach Qia; Qia seized Feng's possessions for maintenance.
translations.idiomatic: Assimilated Miao Long Muqia, elderly, was succeeded by son Feng; grain allotments skipped Qia, who seized Feng's property.

sentences.zh: 俸訴於官，官逮問恰，非罪之也。

translations.literal: Feng complained to officials; officials arrested and questioned Qia, not convicting him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng sued; officials detained Qia but did not convict him.

sentences.zh: 恰輒鎖漢使，已而逐之曰：「速去，此我家事，再來我當以烏雞諸寨踐漢邊矣。

translations.literal: Qia then shackled Han envoys; soon he drove them away saying: "Go quickly—this is my family affair; come again and I shall trample the Han border with Wuji and other stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Qia bound Han envoys and warned them to stay out of a family dispute or face raids from Wuji stockades.

sentences.zh: 」官以計擒之，死獄中。

translations.literal: " Officials captured him by stratagem; he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Officials seized Qia by ruse; he died in jail.

sentences.zh: 無何，龍化龍羊山苗引川苗作亂，曰：「漢無故殺苗，苗請報之。

translations.literal: Before long Longhua Yangyangshan Miao led Sichuan Miao in disorder, saying: "The Han killed Miao without cause; the Miao ask to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Longhua Yangyangshan Miao, allied with Sichuan tribes, cried revenge for Qia's death.

sentences.zh: 」官軍戰不利。

translations.literal: " Government troops fought without success.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops fared poorly.

sentences.zh: 既而都司蔡兆吉招諭令降，待以不死，於是諸苗皆散，俸視事如故。

translations.literal: Soon the regional command's Cai Zhaoji induced them to surrender, treated them with no death penalty; thereupon the various Miao all dispersed; Feng resumed duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhaoji offered amnesty; the Miao dispersed and Feng resumed office.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，平州長官楊進雄兇惡，土人苦之。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Wanli Pingzhou chieftain Yang Jinxiong was fierce and evil; the natives suffered under him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1615 Pingzhou chieftain Yang Jinxiong tyrannized his people.

sentences.zh: 雄無子，以兄繼祿子珂為後，既生子治安，而疏珂。

translations.literal: Xiong had no son; he took his elder brother Jilu's son Ke as heir; having borne son Zhian he then estranged Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted brother Jilu's son Ke, then slighted Ke after son Zhian was born.

sentences.zh: 珂怨雄，雄乃奪珂財產，並其父逐之。

translations.literal: Ke resented Xiong; Xiong therefore seized Ke's property and together with his father drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Ke resented him; Xiong seized his property and expelled him with his father.

sentences.zh: 珂頗得民心，遂為亂，據唐宿坉，攻雄。

translations.literal: Ke had considerable popular support; he therefore rebelled, held Tangxiuchi, and attacked Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke, popular among the people, rebelled from Tangxiuchi and attacked Xiong.

sentences.zh: 雄敗走，屠其家。

translations.literal: Xiong fled in defeat and slaughtered his household.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong fled; Ke massacred his household.

sentences.zh: 各上疏訐奏，詔推問。

translations.literal: Each memorialized accusations; an edict ordered investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides petitioned; the court ordered inquiry.

sentences.zh: 都御史趙釴以雄不法，逮之獄，檄獨山土酋蒙繼武諭珂歸命，許改土為流以安之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhao Kan because Xiong was lawless arrested him in prison and ordered Dushan chieftain Meng Jiwu to persuade Ke to submit, promising to change native to regular office to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Kan jailed Xiong and had Meng Jiwu offer Ke regular office if he submitted.

sentences.zh: 治安計不便，乃陰許以六洞賂繼武借兵。

translations.literal: Zhian judged it disadvantageous; he therefore secretly promised Liudong as bribe to Jiwu to borrow troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhian bribed Jiwu with Liudong lands for troops.

sentences.zh: 繼武乃發兵攻珂，復平州，珂走廣西之泗城。

translations.literal: Jiwu then sent troops to attack Ke, recovered Pingzhou; Ke fled to Sicheng in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwu attacked Ke, retook Pingzhou; Ke fled to Guangxi's Sicheng.

sentences.zh: 繼武遂屯耕六洞地，六洞民不服，復助珂，與繼武相攻。

translations.literal: Jiwu then garrisoned and farmed Liudong land; Liudong people would not submit; they again aided Ke and attacked Jiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiwu colonized Liudong; locals aided Ke against him.

sentences.zh: 珂復據平州。

translations.literal: Ke again held Pingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ke reoccupied Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 巡撫吳嶽招降其父繼祿，六洞乃安。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wu Yue induced Ke's father Jilu to surrender; Liudong was then pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wu Yue won Jilu's surrender and pacified Liudong.

sentences.zh: 平越，古黎峨裏。

translations.literal: Pingyue—in antiquity Li'e Li.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyue was ancient Li'e Li.

sentences.zh: 元為平月長官司。

translations.literal: In Yuan it was the Pingyue native chieftaincy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan it was the Pingyue native office.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年置衛。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu a guard was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1381 a guard was founded.

sentences.zh: 十七年改為軍民指揮使司，屬四川。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year it was changed to an army-and-civilian commander's office, subordinate to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1384 it became an army-civilian command under Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，始置府，置貴州。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period a prefecture was first established and placed in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli a prefecture was created within Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 領州一，曰黃平，即黃平安撫司地。

translations.literal: It oversaw one subprefecture, Huangping—that is, the territory of the Huangping Pacification Superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: It governed Huangping Subprefecture on former Huangping pacification lands.

sentences.zh: 領縣四：曰平越，曰湄潭，曰甕安，即甕水、草塘二長官司地；

translations.literal: It oversaw four counties: Pingyue, Meitan, Weng'an—that is, the territory of the Wengshui and Caotang native chieftaincies;
translations.idiomatic: Counties included Pingyue, Meitan, and Weng'an on Wengshui and Caotang chieftaincy lands;

sentences.zh: 曰余慶，即白泥、余慶二長官司地。

translations.literal: and Yuqing—that is, the territory of the Baini and Yuqing native chieftaincies.
translations.idiomatic: and Yuqing on Baini and Yuqing chieftaincy lands.

sentences.zh: 領長官司一，曰揚義。

translations.literal: It oversaw one native chieftaincy, Yangyi.
translations.idiomatic: One native office, Yangyi, remained under it.

sentences.zh: 初，洪武八年，貴州江力、江松、剌回四十余寨苗把具、播共桶等連結苗、僚二千作亂，平越安撫司乞兵援，命指揮同知胡汝討之。

translations.literal: At first in the eighth year of Hongwu more than forty stockades including Guizhou Jiangli, Jiangsong, and Cihui—Miao Baoju, Bozongtong, and others—linked Miao and Gelao two thousand in disorder; the Pingyue Pacification Superintendent begged troop aid; Commander Assistant Hu Ru was ordered to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1375 forty-odd stockades led by Miao Baoju and Bozongtong, 2,000 strong, rebelled; Pacification Superintendent of Pingyue sought aid; Hu Ru was sent against them.

sentences.zh: 九年，黃平蠻僚都麻堰亂，宣撫司捕之，不克，千戶所以兵討之，亦敗。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Huangping barbarian Gelao at Dumaoyan rebelled; the pacification superintendent captured them but could not overcome them; the centurion office also campaigned and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In 1376 Huangping Gelao at Dumaoyan resisted pacification and defeated centurion troops.

sentences.zh: 乃命重慶諸衛合擊，大破之，平其地。

translations.literal: He then ordered Chongqing guards to combine in attack, greatly defeated them, and pacified the territory.
translations.idiomatic: Chongqing guards combined, routed them, and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 十九年，平越衛麻哈苗楊孟等作亂，命傅友德平之。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Pingyue Guard Maoha Miao Yang Meng and others rebelled; Fu Youde was ordered to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1386 Maoha Miao Yang Meng rebelled at Pingyue; Fu Youde suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 時麻哈長官宋成陣歿，命其子襲。

translations.literal: At the time Maoha chieftain Song Cheng died in battle; his son was ordered to inherit.
translations.idiomatic: Maoha chieftain Song Cheng died in battle; his son inherited.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，察隴、牛場、乾溪苗亂，傅友德平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Chalong, Niuchang, and Qianxi Miao rebelled; Fu Youde pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1389 Chalong, Niuchang, and Qianxi Miao rose; Fu Youde pacified them.

sentences.zh: 二十三年命延安侯唐勝宗往黃平、平越、鎮遠、貴州諸處訓練軍士，提督屯田，相機剿寇。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Yan'an Marquis Tang Shengzong was sent to Huangping, Pingyue, Zhenyuan, and Guizhou to train soldiers, supervise colony fields, and suppress bandits as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: In 1390 Marquis Tang Shengzong trained troops and colony fields across Huangping, Pingyue, Zhenyuan, and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 正統末，鎮遠蠻苗金臺偽稱順天王，與播州苗相煽亂，遂圍平越、新添等衛。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong Zhenyuan barbarian Miao Jintai falsely styled himself Shuntian King, incited disorder with Bozhou Miao, and then besieged Pingyue, Xintian, and other guards.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhengtong, Zhenyuan Miao Jintai styled himself Shuntian King, allied with Bozhou rebels, and besieged Pingyue and Xintian guards.

sentences.zh: 半年城中糧盡，官兵逃者九千余人，貴州東路閉。

translations.literal: After half a year grain in the cities was exhausted; government troops who fled numbered more than nine thousand; Guizhou's eastern route was closed.
translations.idiomatic: After six months cities starved; 9,000 troops deserted; Guizhou's east road was cut.

sentences.zh: 時王驥征麓川，班師過其地，不之顧。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Ji was campaigning in Lucchuan; passing that region he did not attend to it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji, returning from the Luchuan campaign, ignored the crisis.

sentences.zh: 景泰元年命保定伯梁缶佩平蠻將軍印督師進剿，大破之，平八十余寨，擒賊首王阿同等，平越諸衛圍乃解。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingtai he ordered the Earl of Baoding Liang Fu to wear the Pacify Barbarians General seal and supervise the army in advance to suppress them; he greatly defeated them, pacified more than eighty stockades, captured bandit leaders Wang Atong and others, and the sieges of Pingyue guards were then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1450 Earl Liang Fu as Pacify Barbarians General broke 80 stockades, captured Wang Atong, and relieved Pingyue.

sentences.zh: 二年，都御史王來奏，貴州苗韋同烈聚眾於興隆之截洞，復攻平越、清平等衛。

translations.literal: In the second year Censor-in-Chief Wang Lai memorialized that Guizhou Miao Wei Tonglie gathered masses at Jiedong in Xinglong and again attacked Pingyue, Qingping, and other guards.
translations.idiomatic: In 1451 Censor Wang Lai reported Wei Tonglie rallying at Xinglong's Jiedong and raiding Pingyue and Qingping guards.

sentences.zh: 梁缶自沅州發兵由東路，都督方瑛由西路，合兵興隆，擊破之，同烈退保香爐山。

translations.literal: Liang Fu sent troops from Yuanzhou by the eastern route; Commissioner Fang Ying by the western route; united at Xinglong and broke them; Tonglie retreated to defend Xianglushan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Fu advanced from Yuanzhou east, Fang Ying west; united at Xinglong they drove Tonglie to Xianglu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 瑛由龍場，都督陳友由萬潮山，都督毛福壽由重安江，攻破黎樹、翁滿等三百余寨，斬三千余級，招撫袞水等二百余寨，合兵香爐山下。

translations.literal: Ying by Longchang, Commissioner Chen You by Wanchaoshan, Commissioner Mao Fushou by Chong'an River—broke Li Shu, Wengman, and more than three hundred stockades, beheaded more than three thousand, induced Gui shui and more than two hundred stockades to submit, and united below Xianglushan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Ying, Chen You, and Mao Fushou stormed 300 stockades, took 3,000 heads, won 200 surrenders, and converged below Xianglu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 眾縛同烈降，械至京。

translations.literal: The masses bound Tonglie and surrendered; he was caged and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels bound Tonglie and sent him to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 五年，副總兵李貴奏，黎從等寨賊首阿拿、王阿傍、苗金虎等偽號苗王，與銅鼓諸賊相應，乞加兵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Vice Supreme Commander Li Gui memorialized that bandit leaders Ana, Wang A-bang, and Miao Jinhu of Licong and other stockades falsely styled themselves Miao kings and coordinated with Tonggu and other bandits; he begged added troops.
translations.idiomatic: In 1454 Vice Commander Li Gui reported Licong chiefs Ana, Wang A-bang, and Miao Jinhu proclaiming themselves Miao kings and coordinating with Tonggu rebels.

sentences.zh: 七年，巡撫蔣琳奏，剿苗賊於平越，斬四百余級。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Grand Coordinator Jiang Lin memorialized suppressing Miao bandits at Pingyue, beheading more than four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In 1456 Grand Coordinator Jiang Lin reported 400 heads taken at Pingyue.

sentences.zh: 其阿傍等據車碗寨，仍為亂於清平、平越地方，殺指揮王杞，據香爐山，掠偏橋。

translations.literal: A-bang and others held Chewan stockade and still made disorder in Qingping and Pingyue territory, killed Commander Wang Qi, held Xianglushan, and raided Pianqiao.
translations.idiomatic: A-bang held Chewan, killed Commander Wang Qi, seized Xianglu Mountain, and raided Pianqiao.

sentences.zh: 正德十一年命巡撫秦金剿之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhengde he ordered Grand Coordinator Qin Jin to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1516 Grand Coordinator Qin Jin was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 初，黔、楚之交，群苗嘯聚，連寨相望。

translations.literal: At first at the border of Qian and Chu, masses of Miao gathered and cried; linked stockades faced one another.
translations.idiomatic: Along the Guizhou-Huguang frontier Miao stockades lined the hills in revolt.

sentences.zh: 而香爐山周回四十里，高數百尋，四面陡絕，其上平衍，向為叛苗巢穴。

translations.literal: Xianglushan circled forty li, rose hundreds of fathoms, steep on all sides; above it was level and broad; long a nest of rebellious Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianglu Mountain, forty li around and sheer on all sides, had long been a rebel stronghold.

sentences.zh: 阿傍等據之，糾諸寨苗作亂。

translations.literal: A-bang and others held it and mustered stockade Miao for disorder.
translations.idiomatic: A-bang held it and rallied the stockades.

sentences.zh: 巡撫鄒文盛、總兵官李昂等分漢、土兵為五，克其前柵。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Zou Wensheng and Supreme Commander Li Ang and others divided Han and native troops into five and took their forward palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Zou Wensheng and Commander Li Ang took the outer palisade with five columns of Han and native troops.

sentences.zh: 密遣人援崖先登，殺賊守路者，眾蟻附而上，焚賊巢，擒阿傍，余賊猶堅守不下。

translations.literal: Secretly sending men to scale the cliff and ascend first, they killed bandits guarding the road; the masses swarmed up like ants, burned the bandit nests, captured A-bang; remaining bandits still held firm and would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts scaled the cliffs, burned the camp, captured A-bang; holdouts remained above.

sentences.zh: 參將洛忠等詭言招撫，自山後擊之，殲焉。

translations.literal: Assistant Commander Luo Zhong and others falsely spoke of pacification and struck from behind the mountain, annihilating them.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zhong feigned peace then attacked from the rear and annihilated the remnant.

sentences.zh: 遂移師龍頭、黎、蘭等寨，悉破之，賊遂平。

translations.literal: They then moved troops to Longtou, Li, Lan, and other stockades and broke them all; the bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Columns then cleared Longtou, Li, Lan, and other stockades until the rising ended.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，凱裏土司楊世慰叛，合安邦彥兵與平茶群苗來修怨，復窺香爐山，搖動四衛，梗塞糧運。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi Kaili chieftain Yang Shiwei rebelled, united with An Bangyan's troops and Pingcha group Miao to settle old scores, again eyed Xianglushan, shook four guards, and blocked grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In 1624 Kaili chieftain Yang Shiwei joined An Bangyan and Pingcha Miao, threatened Xianglu Mountain, and cut grain convoys to four guards.

sentences.zh: 總督楊述中檄總兵魯欽馳至清平，相機進剿，調副使顏欲章等為後援。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yang Shuzhong ordered Supreme Commander Lu Qin to hurry to Qingping and suppress as circumstances required, transferring Vice Commissioner Yan Yuzhang and others as rear support.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yang Shuzhong rushed Lu Qin to Qingping with Yan Yuzhang in support.

sentences.zh: 欽督將領攻破巖頭，分遣朗溪司田景祥截平茶賊援。

translations.literal: Qin supervised generals in breaking Yantou, separately dispatched Langxi office Tian Jingxiang to intercept Pingcha rebel aid.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qin stormed Yantou and sent Tian Jingxiang to block Pingcha reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 用藥弩及炮殺傷賊眾，賊乘夜遠遁。

translations.literal: Using poisoned crossbows and cannon they killed and wounded bandit masses; the bandits fled far by night.
translations.idiomatic: Poisoned bolts and cannon broke the rebels, who fled by night.

sentences.zh: 自是不敢再窺爐山，四衛得安。

translations.literal: From then they did not dare again to eye Lushan; the four guards were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They never again threatened Xianglu; the four guards were secure.

sentences.zh: 石阡，本思州地。

translations.literal: Shiqian was originally Sizhou territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqian had been Sizhou land.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年置府，隸貴州，領長官司四：曰石阡，曰苗民，曰葛彰葛商，曰龍泉坪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Yongle a prefecture was established, subordinate to Guizhou, overseeing four native chieftaincies: Shiqian, Miaomin, Gezhang Geshang, and Longquanping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1413 a prefecture under Guizhou governed Shiqian, Miaomin, Gezhang Geshang, and Longquanping chieftaincies.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年，葛彰葛商長官安民奏：「前以官鈔糴糧儲備，令蠻民守視。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuande Gezhang Geshang chieftain An Min memorialized: "Previously official notes were used to buy grain for storage and barbarians were ordered to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: In 1431 Gezhang Geshang chieftain An Min noted grain bought with official notes for storage was guarded by tribesmen in remote caves.

sentences.zh: 溪洞險僻，無所支用，恐歲久腐爛，賠納實難，請以充有司祭祀過使廩給之用。

translations.literal: Streams and caves are perilous and remote, with nothing to disburse; fearing rot after years, actual compensation would be difficult; I request using it for regular officials' sacrifices, envoys, and granary provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to use the hoard for official sacrifices and courier rations rather than risk rot and impossible repayment.

sentences.zh: 」縱之。

translations.literal: " This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，改龍泉坪為縣。

translations.literal: In the Wanli period Longquanping was changed to a county.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli Longquanping became a county.

sentences.zh: 新添衛，故麥新地也。

translations.literal: Xintian Guard—formerly Mai-xin territory.
translations.idiomatic: Xintian Guard occupied old Mai-xin land.

sentences.zh: 宋時克麥新地，乃改為新添。

translations.literal: In Song times having conquered Mai-xin territory it was changed to Xintian.
translations.idiomatic: The Song renamed conquered Mai-xin as Xintian.

sentences.zh: 元置新添葛蠻安撫司。

translations.literal: The Yuan established the Xintian Ge Man Pacification Superintendent's office.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan founded the Xintian Ge Man pacification office.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年置長官司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu a native chieftaincy was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1371 a native chieftaincy was created.

sentences.zh: 二十三年改為衛。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year it was changed to a guard.
translations.idiomatic: In 1390 it became a guard.

sentences.zh: 二十九年置新添衛軍民指揮使司，領長官司五：曰新添，曰小平伐，曰把平寨，曰丹平，曰丹行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Xintian Guard army-and-civilian commander's office was established, overseeing five native chieftaincies: Xintian, Xiaopingfa, Bapingzhai, Danping, and Danxing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1396 the army-civilian command oversaw Xintian, Xiaopingfa, Bapingzhai, Danping, and Danxing.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年春，新添安撫宋亦憐真子仁來朝。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year of Hongwu Xintian Pacification Superintendent Song Yilian's son Ren came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 1372 pacification heir Song Ren of Xintian presented himself at court.

sentences.zh: 其秋，平伐、蘆山、山木等砦長來降。

translations.literal: That autumn stockade heads of Pingfa, Lushan, Shanmu, and other stockades came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Pingfa, Lushan, and Shanmu stockades submitted.

sentences.zh: 七年，平伐、谷霞、谷浪等苗攻劫的敖諸寨，指揮僉事張岱討之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Pingfa, Guxia, Gulang, and other Miao attacked and raided De'ao and other stockades; Assistant Commander Zhang Dai campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: In 1374 Pingfa and Guxia Miao raided De'ao; Zhang Dai campaigned against them.

sentences.zh: 岱攻谷峽、剌向關破之，追至的敖，大破之，擒的令、的若而還，蠻大詟。

translations.literal: Dai attacked Guxia and Cixiang Pass and broke them, pursued to De'ao, greatly defeated them, captured Deling and Deruo and returned; the barbarians were greatly awed.
translations.idiomatic: Dai broke Guxia and Cixiang, routed De'ao, captured Deling and Deruo, and awed the tribes.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十四年，貴州巡撫郭子章討平貴州苗，斬獲苗長吳老喬、阿倫、阿皆等十二人，招降男婦甚眾。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Wanli Guizhou Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang suppressed and pacified Guizhou Miao, beheading and capturing Miao leaders Wu Laoqiao, A-lun, A-jie, and twelve others, inducing many men and women to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In 1606 Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang crushed Guizhou Miao, executing chiefs Wu Laoqiao, A-lun, A-jie, and twelve others and accepting mass surrenders.

sentences.zh: 先是，東西二路苗名曰仲家者，盤踞貴龍、平新之間，為諸苗渠帥。

translations.literal: Earlier, eastern and western route Miao called Zhongjia occupied the area between Guilong and Pingxin as chieftains of all Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjia Miao between Guiyang-Longli and Pingyue-Xintian had led east and west route tribes.

sentences.zh: 其在水硍山介於銅仁、思、石者，曰山苗，紅苗之羽翼也，窺黔自平播後財力殫竭，有輕漢心，經年剽掠無虛日。

translations.literal: Those at Shuiyin Mountain between Tongren, Sinan, and Shiqian were called Mountain Miao, wings of the Red Miao; they eyed Qian after Pingbo's finances were exhausted, had contempt for the Han, and raided year-round without idle days.
translations.idiomatic: Shuiyin Mountain Miao between Tongren, Sinan, and Shiqian, allies of the Red Miao, raided daily once Guizhou was drained after the Bozhou campaign.

sentences.zh: 子章奏討之，命相機進兵。

translations.literal: Zizhang memorialized to suppress them; he was ordered to advance troops as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zizhang sought permission and was told to act as needed.

sentences.zh: 子章乃命總兵陳璘、參政洪澄源率官軍五千，益以土兵五千，攻水硍山。

translations.literal: Zizhang then ordered Supreme Commander Chen Lin and Administrator Hong Chengyuan to lead five thousand government troops, adding five thousand native troops, to attack Shuiyin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chen Lin and Hong Chengyuan with 5,000 regulars and 5,000 native troops against Shuiyin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 監軍布政趙健率宣慰土兵萬人，使遊擊劉嶽等督之。

translations.literal: Supervising official Administrator Zhao Jian led ten thousand pacification native troops, with Mobile Corps Commander Liu Yue and others supervising them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jian led 10,000 pacification troops under Liu Yue.

sentences.zh: 及兩路會師，皆九十余日而克。

translations.literal: When the two routes united it took more than ninety days to overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Both columns needed ninety-odd days to prevail.

sentences.zh: 二寇既平，專命總兵陳璘率漢、土兵五千移營新添，進攻東路苗，不一月復克其六箐，諸苗盡平。

translations.literal: After the two foes were pacified he specially ordered Supreme Commander Chen Lin to lead five thousand Han and native troops to move camp to Xintian and attack eastern-route Miao; within one month he again took their six stockades and all Miao were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With Shuiyin and Zhongjia subdued, Chen Lin moved to Xintian, took six eastern stockades in a month, and finished the campaign.

sentences.zh: 金築安撫司，洪武四年，故元安撫密定來朝貢馬，詔賜文綺三匹，置金築長官司，秩正六品，隸四川行省，以密定為長官，世襲。

translations.literal: Jinzhu Pacification Superintendent's office—in the fourth year of Hongwu the former Yuan pacification superintendent Mi Ding came to court presenting horses; an edict bestowed three bolts of patterned silk, established the Jinzhu native chieftaincy, rank 6a, subordinate to the Sichuan provincial administration, with Mi Ding as chieftain in hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: In 1371 former Yuan pacification superintendent Mi Ding presented horses; the Ming created rank-6a Jinzhu chieftaincy under Sichuan with Mi Ding as hereditary chief.

sentences.zh: 十四年敕勞密定曰：「西南諸部雖歸附，然暫入貢而已。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year an edict commended Mi Ding: "Although the southwestern tribes have submitted, they have only entered court temporarily.
translations.idiomatic: In 1381 the emperor praised Mi Ding: southwestern tribes had only paid token homage.

sentences.zh: 爾密定首獻馬五百匹，以助征討，其誠可嘉，故遣特使往諭，俟班師之日，重勞爾功。

translations.literal: You Mi Ding first presented five hundred horses to aid the expedition; your sincerity is commendable; therefore a special envoy is sent to instruct you; when the army returns rewards will again honor your merit.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Ding's gift of 500 horses for the campaign deserved reward after the army's return.

sentences.zh: 」升金築長官司為安撫司，仍以密定為安撫使，予世襲。

translations.literal: " The Jinzhu native chieftaincy was promoted to a pacification superintendent's office; Mi Ding was still pacification superintendent with hereditary tenure.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhu chieftaincy became a pacification office; Mi Ding remained hereditary superintendent.

sentences.zh: 十六年，密定遣使貢方物。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Mi Ding dispatched envoys presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In 1383 Mi Ding sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十八年，密定遣弟保珠來貢。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Mi Ding sent his younger brother Baozhu to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1385 his brother Baozhu tribute at court.

sentences.zh: 二十九年以金築安撫司隸貴州軍民指揮使司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Jinzhu Pacification Superintendent's office was placed under the Guizhou army-and-civilian commander's office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1396 Jinzhu pacification passed to Guizhou command.

sentences.zh: 永樂初年，金築安撫得垛來朝，賜絨錦文綺。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Yongle Pacification Superintendent Deduo of Jinzhu came to court and was given velvet brocade and patterned silk.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongle superintendent Deduo received brocade at court.

sentences.zh: 洪熙、宣德改元，皆貢馬。

translations.literal: At Hongxi and Xuande reign changes horses were presented in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He presented horses at the Hongxi and Xuande enthronements.

sentences.zh: 十年，直隸貴州布政司。

translations.literal: In the tenth year it was directly subordinate to the Guizhou Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1417 it reported directly to Guizhou provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 正統五年，安撫金鏞貢馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengtong Pacification Superintendent Jin Yong presented horses.
translations.idiomatic: In 1440 Superintendent Jin Yong presented horses.

sentences.zh: 成化、弘治、隆慶時歷朝貢。

translations.literal: In Chenghua, Hongzhi, and Longqing successive courts received tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute continued through Chenghua, Hongzhi, and Longqing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十年，吏部覆巡撫胡桂芳奏：「金築安撫土舍金大章乞改土為流，設官建治，欽定州名，鑄給印信，改州判為流官。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year of Wanli the Ministry of Personnel replied to Grand Coordinator Hu Guifang's memorial: "Jinzhu Pacification native clerk Jin Dazhang begs to change native to regular, establish officials and administration, fix the subprefecture name, cast and grant seals, and change the subprefecture judge to a regular official.
translations.idiomatic: In 1612 the Ministry endorsed Hu Guifang's report that Jinzhu clerk Jin Dazhang sought regular administration, new seals, and a circulating vice magistrate.

sentences.zh: 授大章土知州，予四品服色，不許管事。

translations.literal: Grant Dazhang native subprefect; give fourth-rank dress but do not permit administration of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhang would be native subprefect in fourth-rank dress without governing power.

sentences.zh: 子孫承襲，隸州於貴陽府。

translations.literal: Descendants inherit in succession; place the subprefecture under Guiyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs would succeed and the subprefecture would fall under Guiyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 」遂改金築安撫司為廣順州。

translations.literal: " The Jinzhu Pacification Superintendent's office was then changed to Guangshun Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhu pacification was thereby converted to Guangshun Subprefecture.
